## Sheet: `Population Rules`

_21 rows x 5 columns._

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Tell the client the step exists, and when | The whole filing | Mercans, to the client | This is the only rule in this workbook that binds payroll, and it is the one that matters. The balance is declared and paid in April through FR-URSSAF-004; the allocation is a SEPARATE, OPTIONAL act on a different platform, in a window that opens weeks later. Nothing chases the employer. No system reports an error. The only consequence of doing nothing is that a default rule decides where the client's money goes. A client that has never been told will discover this after the window has closed, if at all. | Make it a dated item in the annual client calendar, alongside the April DSN, and repeat it every year - because the window moves, and because the person who knew last year may have changed. The platform's 'rebuild a previous campaign's basket' feature makes acting on the reminder cheap for a client whose policy is stable. |
| Confirm the net-entreprises authorisation covers SOLTeA | Access credentials | Client's net-entreprises account administrator | SOLTeA is entered with net-entreprises credentials - SIRET, surname, first name, password - and the authorisation must have been ACTIVATED. Confirm this while the DSN authorisation is being set up, not in May: an authorisation problem discovered inside a campaign window costs days that the window may not have. | The guide's own troubleshooting rule for a missing SIRET points the same way: if a liable SIRET is not visible in 'Mes SIRET', contact the net-entreprises account administrator to grant the authorisation for it. A missing SIRET is an ACCESS problem, not a liability problem. |
| Do not treat the estimated amount as a declaration | Montant estimatif a repartir | n/a - it is not a payroll figure | Until June an employer may enter the total it estimates it will have to allocate. The guide states plainly that this entry is ESTIMATIVE, that it HAS NO BINDING VALUE for the employer, and that SOLTeA RETAINS ONLY THE ALLOCATION. It is a planning aid. | A build that reconciles this figure against the balance declared in the April DSN is reconciling a non-binding estimate against a declaration, and will report differences that mean nothing. If a reconciliation is wanted, reconcile the April DSN's code 076 against the payroll computation - not against anything in SOLTeA. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Cross-check the SIRETs, and know which failure you are looking at | 'Mes SIRET' against FR-URSSAF-004 | Payroll and the client's net-entreprises administrator | The SIRETs visible in 'Mes SIRET' should be the establishments that declared a balance under code 076 in the April DSN. Where they differ, there are two quite different causes with two quite different remedies: a missing AUTHORISATION, which the guide's troubleshooting note addresses and which the account administrator fixes; or a missing DECLARATION, which is a payroll defect in FR-URSSAF-004 and cannot be fixed here at all. | This is the only useful automated control in this filing, and it is worth running each year before the window opens rather than during it. |
| Grouping has two hard constraints | Mes groupes | Client, in the portal | The guide states both: AT LEAST TWO SIRETs must be added to a group, and A SIRET CANNOT BELONG TO MORE THAN ONE GROUP. Where an employer wants different allocation policies for different parts of the business, that has to be expressed as several disjoint groups, or as per-SIRET allocation for the establishments that differ. | Choose the reference SIRET deliberately: its allocation is duplicated onto every other SIRET in the group, so it is not an arbitrary pick. |
| In-kind grants and SOLTeA allocations are not the same money | Code 077 in FR-URSSAF-004 against the SOLTeA allocation | The client's training and finance functions | In-kind grants of equipment and materials to apprentice training centres remain possible but are NOT managed on SOLTeA. They are declared as a REDUCTION of the balance in the April DSN under code 077. So they reduce the cash balance paid, and therefore reduce what there is to allocate on SOLTeA. Counting the same support in both places overstates what the employer has given. | This is a real risk for a client that supports a training centre both in kind and in cash: the two routes are genuinely different and only one of them appears on the platform. |
| Use the UAI code, not the institution's name | Recherche par code UAI | The client's list of supported institutions | The platform searches by institution name, UAI code, acronym, SIRET or town. Where a client already knows which institutions it supports, capture their UAI CODES. Names are ambiguous, institutions merge and rename, and a wrong selection sends money to somebody else with no way back once the campaign closes. | The same applies to components: an institution with components has a separate information sheet for each, and 'the university' is not the same recipient as one of its institutes. |
| ═══ AMOUNT FORMAT RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| The allocation is in PERCENTAGES, not amounts | Pourcentage de repartition | Client, in the portal | Percentages are entered directly in the selection - the guide records this as a simplification of the current campaign. Because the allocation is proportional, the employer does not need to know the exact balance in order to allocate it, which is why the estimated-amount field can be non-binding without causing a problem. | It also means an allocation made early in the campaign remains valid if the final balance differs from the estimate - the proportions simply apply to the real figure. |
| There is no file format at all | The whole platform | n/a | SOLTeA is a web application. No record layout, no import schema and no export schema was found in the official guide. Column H and column J of the spec sheet say so rather than carrying invented positions. | scope_manifest.json records this filing's format as 'XLSX'. No XLSX template appears in the official guide, which describes a screen-based allocation throughout. Recorded here as online_form with FORMAT TO CONFIRM - see the remarks. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Payroll's duty ends with the declaration; its responsibility does not | The boundary between FR-URSSAF-004 and this filing | Mercans and the client | Payroll computes the 0.09 % balance on the closed preceding year, declares it in the April DSN and pays it. That discharges the obligation. What remains is a business decision the client makes on a platform payroll does not operate - but the client will only know to make it if somebody tells them. Draw the boundary explicitly in the service description rather than leaving it to be discovered. | The asymmetry is worth being clear about with the client: if payroll gets the DECLARATION wrong there is a compliance consequence; if the client misses the ALLOCATION there is no compliance consequence at all, only a lost choice. Both are worth avoiding, for different reasons. |
| Whoever holds the credentials is probably not payroll | Access | Client governance | The decision SOLTeA supports - which training institutions to support - usually belongs to HR, to a training function or to general management, not to payroll. But the credentials are net-entreprises credentials, which payroll administers. Confirm who holds access and who makes the decision, because they are often different people and the gap between them is where the campaign window is missed. | Where Mercans holds the net-entreprises authorisation as service provider, be explicit with the client that holding the credentials is not the same as being mandated to make the allocation. |
| Reuse makes the annual reminder cheap to act on | Panier de repartition similaire a une campagne precedente | Client, in the portal | The platform lets an employer rebuild a previous campaign's allocation basket. For a client whose policy is stable this reduces the annual task to opening the platform and confirming - which is worth saying when the reminder is sent, because 'this will take ten minutes' gets acted on and 'you need to allocate your apprenticeship tax' does not. | It also means the first year's allocation is the one worth spending time on. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Bidirectional constraint | 'Mes SIRET' <-> FR-URSSAF-004 code 076 | Payroll and the net-entreprises administrator | The establishments visible in SOLTeA and the establishments that declared a balance in the April DSN should be the same set. Each names the other: a SIRET in one and not the other is either an authorisation gap or a declaration gap, and the two have different owners. | Run the comparison BEFORE the window opens. Inside the window, an authorisation request competes with the deadline. |
| Bidirectional constraint | Mes groupes - SIRET du groupe <-> SIRET de reference | Client, in the portal | A group needs at least two SIRETs and exactly one reference SIRET, which must be one of them; and no SIRET may belong to a second group. Each of the three group fields names the others. | The reference SIRET's allocation is duplicated onto every other SIRET in the group, so choosing it is a decision rather than a formality. |
| Bidirectional constraint | SOLTeA allocation <-> FR-URSSAF-004 code 077 in-kind grants | The client's training and finance functions | In-kind grants reduce the cash balance under code 077 and are not managed on SOLTeA; the SOLTeA allocation directs the cash balance that remains. Each names the other because a client supporting the same training centre by both routes must not count the support twice. | The guide is explicit that in-kind grants 'demeurent possibles mais ne sont pas gerees sur la plateforme' - possible, but elsewhere. |

## Sheet: `Sample File`

_48 rows x 1 columns._

```text
SOLTeA - repartition du solde de la taxe d'apprentissage (portail employeurs) — SAMPLE FILE
OMITTED - there is nothing to sample. SOLTeA is a WEB APPLICATION: the employer logs in with net-entreprises credentials, searches for institutions, components or courses, and types allocation percentages into its selection. No record layout, no import schema and no export schema appears in the official employer-portal guide held in 00-official-sources/pdfs/soltea_guide.pdf, and none was found elsewhere. Under v2.7 STEP 3.5 and the C25 rule, a fabricated CSV or XLSX for a portal-form filing is an audit failure and would invite an automation of pages that change without notice. Note a correction recorded on the Report Matrix and in the remarks: scope_manifest.json gives this filing's format as 'XLSX', and no XLSX template appears anywhere in the official guide. What this workbook provides instead is the platform's structure and constraints as the guide documents them - the access prerequisite, the SIRET troubleshooting rule, the grouping minimums, the three allocation levels, the search keys, the non-binding status of the estimated amount - which is what someone actually using it needs.

SAMPLE FILE DELIBERATELY NOT PROVIDED - THERE IS NOTHING TO SAMPLE.

SOLTeA IS A WEB APPLICATION, NOT A FILING.

The employer logs in with net-entreprises credentials, searches for
establishments, components or courses, and types allocation
percentages directly into its selection.

No record layout, no import schema and no export schema appears in
the official employer-portal guide, and none was found elsewhere.

A CORRECTION TO scope_manifest.json IS RECORDED HERE:

The manifest gives this filing's format as 'XLSX'. No XLSX template
appears anywhere in the official guide, which describes a
screen-based allocation throughout. Under v2.7 STEP 3.5 the channel
is recorded here as online_form, with FORMAT TO CONFIRM. This
should be carried back into the manifest.

If a bulk import DOES exist for employers with very many
establishments, it is not documented in the guide obtained. That is
worth confirming with the Caisse des Depots for a large client -
but note that the GROUPING feature already solves most of that
problem by duplicating one reference SIRET's allocation across a
group.

WHAT IS PROVIDED INSTEAD, AND IS WHAT A USER ACTUALLY NEEDS:

- the access prerequisite (net-entreprises credentials, activated
authorisation) and the guide's own troubleshooting rule for a
missing SIRET;
- the grouping mechanics and their two hard constraints;
- the three levels a recipient can be chosen at, and the search
keys - including the UAI code, which is the only reliable one;
- the direct percentage entry, and the explicitly NON-BINDING
status of the estimated amount;
- the boundary with FR-URSSAF-004: what is declared and paid there
and what is merely directed here, and the in-kind grants that
never reach this platform at all.

THE MOST PERISHABLE FACT IN THIS WORKBOOK:

THE CAMPAIGN DATES. FR-CCG-001 Module 10 records the 2026 window as
26 May to 21 October. They move every year. Confirm them on the
platform each spring rather than relying on any document.
```

## Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

_31 rows x 3 columns._

**Declaration d'accident du travail ou d'accident de trajet (DAT) - cerfa 14463*03 / S6200 — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY**

**What the employer must declare when an employee is injured, to whom, and inside what is one of the shortest deadlines in European payroll - 48 hours from LEARNING of the accident, not from the accident. Two things make this filing harder than it looks. Most of the form is HSE and line-management data rather than payroll data, so a 48-hour clock has to cross two functions. And the employer must also hand the victim the accident sheet, so that they can be treated without paying - a separate obligation, with its own fine, that leaves no trace in any system.**

| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
|---|---|---|
| ═══ WHAT MUST BE DECLARED ═══ |  |  |
| An accident occurring by the fact of, or on the occasion of, work | YES | The core case. Ticked as 'D'ACCIDENT DU TRAVAIL' in the form's title, with the circumstances block identifying where and when. |
| An accident on the journey between home and work | YES | But as an ACCIDENT DE TRAJET - the form's title carries a separate tick-box for it. The distinction is not cosmetic: it changes how the accident bears on the employer's own occupational-risk rate. |
| An accident on the journey between work and the place of the meal | YES | The circumstances block provides for it explicitly, as it does for the meal place itself and for travel undertaken for the employer. |
| An accident with NO work stoppage | YES | The consequences block has a 'SANS ARRET DE TRAVAIL' box. The declaration is still due within 48 hours, and the victim still needs the accident sheet in order to be treated without paying. A process that only declares accidents that produce absence misses these entirely - and they are the majority. |
| An accident causing death | YES | The consequences block has a 'DECES' box. |
| An accident to an agency worker | YES | Declared by the AGENCY, which is the employer - the notice is explicit. The USER company instead completes form S6209, 'information prealable a la declaration d'accident du travail', immediately. Two forms, two parties, one accident. |
| A minor accident already entered in the register of minor accidents | PARTIAL | Where the employer keeps such a register and the accident was entered in it, no declaration follows unless it turns out to be more than minor - at which point the declaration is made and the register entry date and number are quoted on it. The form carries the fields for exactly that case. |
| An occupational disease | NO | A different procedure with a different form and different time limits. This form is for accidents. A stoppage for occupational disease is still signalled in the DSN under its own reason code (FR-DSN-003). |
| ═══ WHO DECLARES, AND TO WHOM ═══ |  |  |
| The employer of the establishment of permanent attachment | YES | The form's own block heading. Note that this may not be where the accident happened - the accident block carries a separate SIRET for the place of the accident where it differs. |
| The CPAM of the victim's HABITUAL RESIDENCE | YES | Not the fund of the employer's establishment. This is why the victim's home address on the form has procedural consequence: it determines the recipient. |
| The CARSAT and the labour inspectorate | YES | Each receives one of the three volets sent. The CARSAT copy is what connects the accident to the establishment's occupational-risk record - and therefore to its future contribution rate. |
| The user company, for an agency worker | NO | It completes the S6209 preliminary information form instead. The agency, as employer, makes the declaration. |
| ═══ WHAT ELSE THE EMPLOYER MUST DO ═══ |  |  |
| Give the victim the accident sheet (feuille d'accident) | YES | The fourth volet, which the form instructs the employer to KEEP when sending the first three. It lets the victim obtain care without advancing the cost. Failing to deliver it is punished by a fine alongside failing to declare - it is a separate obligation with a separate sanction. |
| Complete the salary attestation S6202 where there is a stoppage | YES | The form's own asterisked warning: if the accident caused a stoppage, complete the attestation IMMEDIATELY so the fund can compute the daily benefits. And the notice adds: a further stoppage after a period of care or a return to work, IN A DIFFERENT MONTH, requires the same formality again. |
| File the DSN work-stoppage signal | YES | FR-DSN-003, within 5 days. A third obligation from the same event, on a third deadline. The 48-hour one falls first. |
| Substantiate any reservations within 10 clear days | YES | Where reservations are entered on the declaration. Reservations entered and never substantiated are worse than none at all: they delay the employee's recognition without protecting the employer. |
| Pay the victim's medical costs | NO | The occupational-risk branch pays in full, which is what the accident sheet enables. The employer's exposure is through its future contribution rate, not through the treatment. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| An accident in an establishment other than the victim's own | YES | The accident block carries a separate SIRET for the place of the accident. The declaring employer remains the establishment of attachment. |
| An employee of an employer grouping | YES | The notice requires the SIRET of the establishment the victim was working for at the time of the accident. |
| An accident caused by a third party | YES | The notice makes reporting it IMPERATIVE whatever the third party's share of responsibility, because it is how the fund recovers from the third party rather than from the employer's risk account. |
| An accident with several victims | YES | One declaration per victim, each on its own 48-hour clock and each with its own accident sheet. The 'other victims' box records that others exist; it does not declare them. |
| An accident the employer believes is not occupational | YES | Declare it anyway, within 48 hours, and enter reservations. There is no route by which an employer decides not to declare because it disagrees - the fund decides, and reservations are how the employer is heard. |

## Sheet: `File Structure`

_154 rows x 1 columns._

```text
Declaration d'accident du travail ou d'accident de trajet (DAT) - cerfa 14463*03 / S6200 — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

═══ CHANNEL AND DISTRIBUTION - v2.7 STEP 3.5, VERIFIED ═══
Channel   : online_form through net-entreprises.fr (service
IDAT), or paper by REGISTERED LETTER WITH
ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF RECEIPT.
Recipient : the CPAM of the victim's HABITUAL RESIDENCE - not of
the employer's establishment. This is why the
victim's home address on the form has procedural
consequence.
Volets    : the form instructs the employer to send the FIRST
THREE volets and KEEP THE FOURTH. The notice names
the three recipients:

volet 1  ->  CPAM
volet 2  ->  CARSAT
(CRAMIF in Ile-de-France, CGSS
in the overseas departments)
volet 3  ->  Inspection du travail
volet 4  ->  KEPT, then given to the VICTIM

The CARSAT copy is the one that reaches the establishment's
occupational-risk record, and therefore its future contribution
rate. See FR-CARSAT-001.

Centralised management: the notice records that a company
managing work accidents centrally may register a correspondence
address through the electronic service, after which no mail goes
to the establishment of attachment and mail sent to the
correspondence address IS OPPOSABLE. Useful, and worth
confirming with any client that uses it, because opposability
means deadlines run from delivery there.

═══ THE FORM - FIVE PRINTED BLOCKS ═══
cerfa 14463*03 (S6200), notice 50261#04
Two title tick-boxes:  D'ACCIDENT DU TRAVAIL  /
D'ACCIDENT DE TRAJET

1  L'EMPLOYEUR (etablissement d'attache permanent de la victime)
name or company name | address | postcode | telephone
SIRET of the establishment of attachment
N° de risque Securite Sociale
occupational health service: name | address | postcode

2  LA VICTIME
social security number (or, failing that, sex + DOB)
name: FAMILY NAME AT BIRTH then used name
address | postcode
nationality: Francaise / EEE, Suisse / Autre
date of hire | occupation
qualification | seniority IN THE POST
contract: CDI / CDD / Apprenti-Eleve / Interimaire / Autre

3  LES INFORMATIONS RELATIVES A L'ACCIDENT
date | time (H, mn)
place, or name and address of the site (chantier)
SIRET of the place of the accident, where it differs
circumstances - six boxes
activity of the victim | nature of the accident
object whose contact injured
EVENTUELLES RESERVES MOTIVEES
site of injuries | nature of injuries
transported to | other victims? OUI/NON
working hours that day: de..a.. ET de..a..
accident recorded on | at | by whom (3 boxes)
entry in the register of minor accidents: date | number
consequences: SANS ARRET / AVEC ARRET (*) / DECES
police report? NON / OUI, by whom

4  LE TEMOIN ou LA PREMIERE PERSONNE AVISEE
name | address | postcode

5  LE TIERS
caused by a third party? OUI / NON
if OUI: name and address | its insurer

Signature: signatory name | capacity | place | date

═══ THE CLOCK, AND WHY IT IS SHORTER THAN IT LOOKS ═══
48 HOURS, not counting Sundays and public holidays, from the
employer HAVING LEARNED OF THE ACCIDENT.

Two features make it shorter in practice than it reads:

- it runs from KNOWLEDGE, so it can start before payroll or HR
has been told anything - a supervisor who is told at 17:00
on Thursday has started the clock;

- most of the form is HSE and line-management data, not
payroll data, so a 48-hour deadline has to cross at least
two functions, out of hours as well as in.

Reservations, if entered, add a second clock: TEN CLEAR DAYS
after the declaration to substantiate them with the fund.

Compare the parallel obligations arising from the same event:

this declaration            48 hours
salary attestation S6202    'immediately', and again for any
new stoppage in a DIFFERENT month
DSN stoppage signal         5 days   (FR-DSN-003)

None of the three discharges another.

═══ WHAT ELSE THE EVENT SETS OFF ═══
FORM S6202 - attestation de salaire accident du travail ou
maladie professionnelle. Required where the accident caused a
work stoppage, and the form's own asterisk says 'immediately'.
It is what lets the fund compute the daily benefits, which are
paid at higher rates than ordinary sickness and with no waiting
period. The notice adds that a NEW stoppage after a period of
care or a return to work, IN A DIFFERENT MONTH, requires the
attestation again.

FORM S6209 - information prealable a la declaration d'accident
du travail. Where the victim is an agency worker made available
to a user company, the USER COMPANY completes S6209
immediately, and the AGENCY - as the employer - makes the
declaration on the present form. Two parties, two forms, one
accident. Note the SIRET consequence: the employer SIRET is the
agency BRANCH where the victim is registered, and the
place-of-accident SIRET is the user establishment.

FR-DSN-003 - the DSN work-stoppage signal, within 5 days, with
an occupational stoppage reason and the accident date in
S21.G00.60.012.

FR-CARSAT-001 - not an action, a consequence: the accident
reaches the establishment's occupational-risk record through the
CARSAT volet and bears on its FUTURE contribution rate.

═══ SANCTIONS - TWO OMISSIONS, ONE FINE ═══
The notice states it in terms, citing Social Security Code arts.
L114-17-1, L471-1 and R471-3: a fine is imposed on employers who
have neglected

- to declare the accident to the primary fund within 48
hours, OR
- to deliver the ACCIDENT SHEET to the victim.

Two distinct omissions, one sanction. The second is the one an
electronic-only process forgets, because filing through
net-entreprises produces no paper volet to hand over.

The notice adds two further exposures:

- the primary fund MAY DEMAND REIMBURSEMENT OF THE WHOLE OF
the expenditure incurred on the accident, and impose a
financial penalty;

- fraud or false declaration is punishable by financial
penalties, a fine and/or imprisonment (Penal Code arts.
313-1 to 313-3, 433-19, 441-1 and following; Social
Security Code art. L114-17-1).
```

## Sheet: `Population Rules`

_23 rows x 5 columns._

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| The 48-hour clock starts on KNOWLEDGE, and the form records when | Accident constate le ... heure ... / par qui | HSE and line management | The declaration is due within 48 hours, NOT COUNTING SUNDAYS AND PUBLIC HOLIDAYS, after the employer has learned of the accident. The form asks for the date and time the accident was recorded and how it became known - observed by the employer, by its staff, or described by the victim. Record this CONTEMPORANEOUSLY: it is the employer's only evidence that the declaration was in time, and it cannot be reconstructed credibly afterwards. | An accident that happens on a Friday evening and is reported to the employer on Monday morning starts its clock on Monday. One that happens on Monday and is reported the same day is due by Wednesday. The process must therefore capture the knowledge event, not only the accident event. |
| The risk number is not a payroll parameter | N° de risque Securite Sociale | The AT/MP rate notification - FR-CARSAT-001 | The notice states where it comes from: the risk number APPEARING ON THE NOTIFICATION OF THE RATE applicable to the activity under which the victim's salary is accounted. It is therefore an inbound datum, held per establishment, refreshed whenever the establishment is reclassified. Where one establishment carries several activities with different risk numbers, the one to declare is the one the victim's salary is booked under. | A stale risk number attaches the accident to the wrong risk category, which distorts the establishment's own experience rating - and the effect is on the FUTURE contribution rate, so it is invisible for a year or more. |
| Three fields payroll does not hold | Qualification professionnelle, anciennete dans le poste, nationalite (banded) | HR, and in the case of post seniority often nobody | The occupational qualification uses the notice's own eight-value statistical classification, which is not the collective-agreement grade payroll holds. The seniority is IN THE POST, in five bands - not seniority in the company, which is what payroll holds. The nationality is a three-way band, not a country. All three must be mapped or sourced explicitly before the first accident, not improvised during one. | Post seniority is the one most often held nowhere at all. If the client cannot say when an employee took up their current post, this field cannot be answered accurately - and that is worth telling the client while there is time to start recording it. |
| Circumstances decide work accident versus commuting accident | The six circumstance boxes and the two title boxes | A legal characterisation, made on advice - not by payroll | The form's title carries two tick-boxes, 'D'ACCIDENT DU TRAVAIL' and 'D'ACCIDENT DE TRAJET', and the circumstances block carries six boxes that place the accident: usual workplace, occasional workplace, meal place, home-to-work journey, work-to-meal journey, or travel for the employer. The classification has lasting financial consequence, because a commuting accident does not bear on the employer's own risk rate in the same way as a workplace accident. | This must not be decided by whoever happens to be filling in the form. Confirm who makes the call and on what basis, and record the reasoning - because if the fund takes a different view, the employer's own file is the starting point for contesting it. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| The DSN does not discharge this obligation | FR-DSN-003 against this declaration | Client process design | A DSN work-stoppage signal carrying an occupational reason - work accident, commuting accident or occupational disease - reports the ABSENCE. It does not declare the ACCIDENT. The two obligations have different deadlines (5 days against 48 hours), different recipients and different content, and the shorter one falls first. A build that emits the stoppage signal and considers the event handled has missed the declaration entirely. | The reverse error also occurs: declaring the accident and omitting the stoppage signal, which leaves the daily benefits unopened. One event, three artifacts - this declaration within 48 hours, the S6202 salary attestation immediately, and the DSN stoppage signal within 5 days. |
| Reservations are admissible on two grounds only | Eventuelles reserves motivees | Legal or HR, on advice | The notice cites art. R441-11: reservations can be taken into account ONLY if they bear on the circumstances of TIME AND PLACE of the accident, or on the existence of a cause TOTALLY UNCONNECTED with the work. Anything else - a belief that the victim was careless, a doubt about the severity - is not a ground and will not be considered. Where reservations are entered, the employer has TEN CLEAR DAYS after the declaration to substantiate them with the fund. | Reservations entered and never substantiated are worse than none: they suspend the employee's recognition, damage the relationship, and protect nothing. Confirm who may enter them and that they know the ten-day deadline before enabling the field at all. |
| The accident sheet is a separate obligation with its own sanction | Volet 4 - la feuille d'accident | HR or line management | The notice records that the fine under Social Security Code arts. L114-17-1, L471-1 and R471-3 attaches to employers who have neglected to declare within 48 hours OR TO DELIVER THE ACCIDENT SHEET TO THE VICTIM. Two omissions, one sanction. The sheet is what lets the victim be treated without advancing the cost, so failing to hand it over has an immediate practical effect on the injured person as well as a legal one. | This is the obligation an electronic process forgets, because filing through net-entreprises produces no paper volet. Confirm explicitly how the client gets the accident sheet to the victim when the declaration is electronic. |
| A stoppage triggers the salary attestation immediately | Consequences: AVEC ARRET DE TRAVAIL, and form S6202 | Payroll | The form's asterisked note: if the accident caused a stoppage, complete the S6202 salary attestation IMMEDIATELY, so that the fund can compute the daily benefits. The notice adds that a NEW stoppage after a period of care or after a return to work, falling in a DIFFERENT MONTH, requires the attestation again. So it is not a one-off per accident: it recurs per stoppage per month. | This is where payroll's real involvement in an occupational accident begins. The benefit rates are higher than ordinary sickness and there is no waiting period, so an attestation delivered late or on ordinary-sickness assumptions underpays the employee. |
| ═══ AMOUNT FORMAT RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| This declaration carries no amounts at all | The whole form | n/a | There is not one monetary field on the cerfa. The employer declares facts, circumstances and times; the fund computes everything financial. The money appears in two other places: the S6202 salary attestation, which gives the fund the reference pay for computing daily benefits, and the employer's own AT/MP contribution rate, which the accident affects prospectively through FR-CARSAT-001. | The formatting rules that DO matter are time ones. The accident time is asked in hours and minutes; the victim's working hours on the day are asked as TWO ranges, which accommodates a split day with a meal break. A single range cannot represent the ordinary French working day and would misplace an accident occurring over the lunch period. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Most of this form is not payroll's to fill | Blocks 3, 4 and 5 | HSE, line management, legal | Of the five blocks, payroll can supply the employer block and most of the victim block. The accident block, the witness block and the third-party block are HSE and line-management data, and the reservations field is a legal act. The right design is a form assembled from two sources with clear ownership of each field, not a payroll extract with gaps. | The consequence for the deadline is important: a 48-hour clock across two functions needs a defined handover, out of hours as well as in. Confirm at implementation who completes the form on a Friday evening. |
| Feed the risk number in, do not hold it locally | N° de risque Securite Sociale | FR-CARSAT-001 | The risk number and the AT/MP rate arrive together in the establishment's rate notification. Store both per SIRET, with their effective dates, and read this field from that store. Do not let it be typed on the form from memory, and do not let it be inherited from a template of a previous declaration. | The same store serves the payroll contribution calculation and this declaration, which is a useful consistency check: if the two disagree, one of them has been maintained by hand. |
| Three artifacts, three clocks, one event | This declaration, S6202, FR-DSN-003 | Payroll and HSE jointly | An occupational accident with a stoppage produces: this declaration within 48 hours; the S6202 salary attestation immediately; and the DSN work-stoppage signal within 5 days. They go to overlapping but different places, they carry different content, and none of them discharges another. Build the process as one trigger with three outputs rather than three processes that happen to share a cause. | The commonest real-world failure is the reverse of the one people expect: not forgetting the DSN, which is automated, but forgetting the 48-hour declaration, which is manual - and it is the one with the criminal-adjacent sanction attached. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Bidirectional constraint | Date et heure de l'accident <-> Horaire de travail de la victime le jour de l'accident | HSE and time-and-attendance | The accident time read against the two declared working ranges is what establishes whether the accident occurred during working time. Neither is meaningful alone for that purpose, and each names the other in its Conditional Reason. | An accident timed outside both declared ranges is not necessarily wrong - it may be travel for the employer, or a meal break, both of which the circumstances block provides for - but it should be reconciled deliberately before filing rather than discovered by the fund. |
| Bidirectional constraint | SIRET de l'etablissement d'attache <-> SIRET du lieu de l'accident | HSE and establishment master data | The place-of-accident SIRET is conditional on the accident having occurred somewhere other than the establishment of attachment - or on the declaration being made by a temporary work agency, or the victim being employed by an employer grouping. The two SIRETs answer different questions and each names the other. | For an agency declaration the notice requires the agency BRANCH where the victim is registered as the employer SIRET and the USER establishment as the place SIRET. Getting them the wrong way round attributes the accident to the wrong risk account. |
| Bidirectional constraint | Consequences (AVEC ARRET) <-> form S6202 and FR-DSN-003 | Payroll | Ticking 'with work stoppage' creates two further obligations immediately: the S6202 salary attestation and the DSN stoppage signal. The tick is the trigger and the two artifacts are its consequences, so the constraint reads outward from this field rather than between two fields on the same form. | The notice's own addition matters here: a NEW stoppage after care or after a return to work, in a DIFFERENT MONTH, requires the attestation again. So the trigger is not once-per-accident. |
| Bidirectional constraint | Reserves motivees <-> the circumstances of time and place | Legal or HR | Art. R441-11 admits reservations only on the circumstances of time and place, or on a cause totally unconnected with the work. The circumstances declared in block 3 are therefore the ground on which any reservation must stand, and the two must be consistent: reservations that contradict the employer's own declared circumstances defeat themselves. | The ten-clear-day substantiation deadline runs from the declaration, not from the accident, so entering reservations shortens an already short process. |
| Bidirectional constraint | L'accident a-t-il ete cause par un tiers ? <-> Un rapport de police a-t-il ete etabli ? | HSE | Both relate to the involvement of somebody outside the employment relationship, and a police report most often exists precisely where a third party does. Each names the other. | The third-party question is the one with financial consequence for the employer: it is how the fund recovers its outlay from the third party instead of charging the employer's own risk account. The notice's threshold - 'whatever their share of responsibility' - is deliberately low. |

| ═══ THE THREE FIELDS PAYROLL CANNOT SUPPLY ═══ |  |  |  |
| Qualification professionnelle : Technicien | Qualification professionnelle | One of the notice's eight statistical classes: cadre, technicien, agent de maitrise, employe, apprenti, eleve de l'enseignement technique, ouvrier non qualifie, ouvrier qualifie. | NOT the collective-agreement grade payroll holds. Map the client's grade structure onto these eight once, and have it signed off. |
| Anciennete dans le poste de travail : un an et plus | Anciennete dans le poste de travail | One of five bands: less than a week, a week to under a month, a month to under three months, three months to under a year, a year and more. | Seniority IN THE POST, not in the company. A twenty-year employee moved to a new post last week is in the FIRST band. Most clients hold this nowhere at all. |
| Nationalite : [X] Francaise | Nationalite | One of three bands only - Francaise, EEE/Suisse, Autre. | The form does not ask for the nationality itself. Payroll usually holds a country, which is a three-way mapping to define once. |
| ═══ WHAT TICKING 'WITH STOPPAGE' SETS OFF ═══ |  |  |  |
| [X] AVEC ARRET DE TRAVAIL (*) | Consequences | The form's own asterisk: 'Important, si l'accident a entraine un arret, remplissez immediatement l'attestation de salaire S 6202.' | Two further obligations from this one tick: the S6202 attestation immediately, and the DSN stoppage signal FR-DSN-003 within 5 days. | ═══ THE VOLET NOBODY SENDS ANYWHERE ═══ |  |  |  |
| Volets 1, 2 and 3 -> CPAM, CARSAT (or CRAMIF / CGSS), inspection du travail | Distribution printed on the form | The first three volets go out, by registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt on the paper route. | The CARSAT copy is what connects the accident to the establishment's occupational-risk record, and therefore to its future contribution rate. |
| Volet 4 -> kept by the employer, then given to the VICTIM | La feuille d'accident | The accident sheet. It lets the victim obtain care WITHOUT paying. | Failing to deliver it is punished by a fine ALONGSIDE failing to declare (arts. L114-17-1, L471-1, R471-3). ## Sheet: `Sample File`

_47 rows x 1 columns._

```text
Declaration d'accident du travail ou d'accident de trajet (DAT) - cerfa 14463*03 / S6200 — SAMPLE FILE
OMITTED - and correctly so under v2.7 STEP 3.5, because the channel is a FORM rather than a file. This declaration is made either on the cerfa form itself, sent by registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt, or through the net-entreprises online service (IDAT), which the notice records as teletransmitting it directly to the fund. No field-level specification of the IDAT service was obtained, and no official sample file exists in FR-compliance/00-official-sources/sample-files/. Fabricating a CSV or XML for a filing that has no published file format would be a C25 audit failure. What IS provided instead is better for a developer: the complete form, block by block and caption by caption, on the spec sheet, with the notice's own enumerated value lists on the Field Options sheet - all read off cerfa 14463*03 itself, which is held in 00-official-sources/pdfs/ as dat_s6200_14463.pdf and can be opened alongside this workbook.

SAMPLE FILE DELIBERATELY NOT PROVIDED - THE CHANNEL IS A FORM.

VERIFIED CHANNEL (v2.7 STEP 3.5):

Channel   : online_form - the net-entreprises electronic service,
named IDAT in the notice, which teletransmits the
declaration directly to the fund;
or PAPER, by registered letter with acknowledgement of
receipt.
Portal    : net-entreprises.fr
Recipient : the CPAM of the victim's HABITUAL RESIDENCE.
Copies to the CARSAT (CRAMIF in Ile-de-France, CGSS
overseas) and the labour inspectorate.
Form      : cerfa 14463*03, reference S6200; notice 50261#04.
Volets    : send the first THREE. KEEP THE FOURTH and give it to
the victim - it is the feuille d'accident.
Status    : CONFIRMED for channel, portal, recipients and volets.
FORMAT TO CONFIRM for the IDAT field layout, which was
not obtained.

A USEFUL FEATURE OF THE ELECTRONIC SERVICE, from the notice:

A company with CENTRALISED management of work accidents can set a
correspondence address to which all mail is sent. In that case no
further mail goes to the establishment of attachment, and mail sent
to the correspondence address IS OPPOSABLE - which cuts both ways,
and is worth confirming with any client that uses it.

WHY NOTHING IS INVENTED:

There is no published file format for this declaration. A
fabricated CSV or XML would be a C25 audit failure and would be
used to build an interface to a channel that accepts no such file.

WHAT IS PROVIDED INSTEAD:

- the complete form, block by block, caption by caption, on the
spec sheet, with column B carrying the printed French captions
verbatim;
- the notice's own enumerated value lists - qualification classes,
seniority bands, injury sites, circumstance boxes - on the Field
Options sheet;
- the form itself, in 00-official-sources/pdfs/dat_s6200_14463.pdf,
which can be opened alongside this workbook.
```

Design retrieval around the payroll cut-off with margin rather than around a single published figure. |  |  |  |

## Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

_28 rows x 3 columns._

**BPIJ - bordereau de paiement des indemnites journalieres (inbound) — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY**

**Where the money from a work stoppage becomes visible. The stoppage signal FR-DSN-003 carries NOT ONE AMOUNT - the employer declares facts and dates and the fund computes the benefits - so this statement is the only place the employer sees what was actually paid. It serves two opposite purposes depending on one flag declared in that other filing: a remittance advice for a subrogated employer, and the source of an amount a non-subrogated employer needs but never receives. Both must be built, and the overpayments the fund reclaims must be read alongside the payments.**

| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
|---|---|---|
| ═══ WHO NEEDS IT ═══ |  |  |
| A subrogated employer | YES | Essential. The fund pays the benefits to the employer, typically as one credit covering many employees, and the BPIJ is what decomposes it. Without it the employer has money it cannot allocate. |
| A non-subrogated employer | PARTIAL | It still needs the AMOUNT, because it must compute a top-up net of benefits it never receives. But the guide frames the service around SUBROGATED benefits paid to the employer's account, and whether a non-subrogated employer sees useful data here is not established - it is a client-specific question. Where the answer is no, the amount must come from the employee's own benefit statement. |
| An employer with no absences | NO | Nothing to see. But the registration should still exist before it is needed - see the access prerequisite. |
| An employer whose employees are affiliated to many funds | YES | And this is the normal case, because affiliation follows the employee's residence. The guide provides searching BY CPAM for exactly this reason. A dispersed workforce means many payment streams to reconcile. |
| ═══ WHAT IT CARRIES ═══ |  |  |
| The benefits paid, per employee | YES | The payload. The guide describes the service as the reflection of the daily benefits paid by the sickness insurance. |
| The period each payment covers | YES | Which is what allows the benefit to be allocated to the right payroll period rather than to the month it arrived. |
| The accounting day and the payment date | YES | Named among the criteria the data can be read by, and the key that ties a line to a bank credit. |
| Overpayments being reclaimed (indus) | YES | Documented with their own search screens in both views. For a subrogated employer an indu is money going back OUT for an absence already settled in payroll. |
| The employee's affiliating fund | YES | A search dimension, and the explanation for why receipts arrive from many sources. |
| Why a benefit is the amount it is | NO | The fund computes the benefit from the pay history it holds. The BPIJ reports what was paid, not the calculation behind it. An employer that disputes an amount takes it up with the fund. |
| Anything about the stoppage itself | NO | The stoppage is declared in FR-DSN-003 and this statement answers it with money. The two are complementary and neither contains the other's content. |
| ═══ HOW IT IS OBTAINED ═══ |  |  |
| Consulted on the portal | YES | Available 7 days a week, 24 hours a day, with the settlement consultable about 2 days after the fund pays. |
| Exported for integration into payroll software | YES | To .csv, .xls, .pdf and .xml. The guide is explicit that the exports exist so they can be integrated into payroll software - which is an invitation to automate that this workbook can only partly answer, because no column specification is published. |
| Pushed to the employer | NO | Nothing arrives. Somebody must look, or something must fetch. |
| Available indefinitely | NO | The guide states data are visible for 33 MONTHS. That is generous but finite, and it is shorter than some payroll retention obligations - so anything needed as evidence beyond that must be exported and kept. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| A benefit that arrives after the payroll for its period has run | YES | The normal case rather than the exception, and the reason the engine must be able to regularise a prior period. Allocating benefits to the month of receipt makes the top-up calculations unexplainable. |
| An employer with several establishments grouped for payment | YES | The stoppage signal provides a centralising SIRET for exactly this (FR-DSN-003, S21.G00.60.600), and the BPIJ can be searched by SIRET. Where the centralising SIRET was not declared, the fund settles per establishment and the reconciliation is against several streams. |
| An indu on an absence already closed in payroll | YES | The fund reclaims; payroll must regularise the affected period. A process that reads only payments sees an unexplained bank debit. |
| An employee affiliated to a fund outside the general scheme | NO | Out of scope for this build. Note that one of the source documents in the pack is from a special scheme's own fund, which offers its own BPIJ on the same portal but on its own terms - and states that its salary attestations cannot be filed through the platform at all. A reminder that BPIJ availability and behaviour follow the SCHEME, not the portal. |

## Sheet: `File Structure`

_178 rows x 1 columns._

```text
BPIJ - bordereau de paiement des indemnites journalieres (inbound) — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

═══ WHAT THE BPIJ IS, AND WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS ═══
From the guide's own definition: the BPIJ is

« le reflet des paiements des indemnites journalieres versees
par l'Assurance Maladie »

and it lets the employer consult

« le detail des reglements effectues sur le compte de
l'employeur concernant les indemnites journalieres
subrogees de ses salaries »

It matters because of what the STOPPAGE SIGNAL does not carry.
FR-DSN-003 has NOT ONE AMOUNT RUBRIQUE: the employer declares
who, when, why and where to pay, and the fund computes the
benefits itself from the pay history it already holds through
the monthly DSN.

So the BPIJ is the ONLY place the employer ever sees what was
actually paid.

An implementation that builds FR-DSN-003 and stops has built the
half that costs the client nothing, and skipped the half that
reconciles its money.

═══ ACCESS - THE PREREQUISITE THAT IS A DIFFERENT SERVICE FROM THE ONE YOU WOULD EXPECT ═══
Portal : net-entreprises.fr

Path   : 1. click « Attestation de salaire »
2. click « Bordereaux de paiement des indemnites
journalieres »
3. the BPIJ interface opens

THE PREREQUISITE: registration for the SALARY-ATTESTATION
service. The guide states that a DSN-filing company can also
follow its BPIJ from the DSN dashboard - but ONLY:

« a condition d'etre inscrit a l'attestation de salaire
pour le versement des indemnites journalieres »

A second source in the pack puts it from the other direction:
if the « Attestations » tab is absent, the employer must first
register for the salary-attestation and payment-statement
services.

FILING DSNs IS NOT SUFFICIENT. This is the prerequisite most
likely to be missing, precisely because it is not the service
a reader would expect to need. For a SUBROGATED client the
consequence is immediate and silent: credits arriving in the
bank account with no statement to decompose them.

Check it at onboarding for any client with subrogation.

Availability : 7 days a week, 24 hours a day. The settlement is
consultable about 2 DAYS after the fund pays -
though a second fund's note gives 3 to 4 days
for its own population, so it VARIES BY FUND.
Retention    : data visible for 33 MONTHS.

═══ HOW THE DATA ARE ORGANISED - TWO VIEWS AND FOUR EXPORTS ═══
SEARCH DIMENSIONS documented by the guide:

by CPAM d'affiliation of the employee
by SIRET and dates
by employee
by journee comptable (reimbursement day)
by date

TWO VIEWS:

« vue BPIJ »      organised by remittance - the finance
view, for reconciling a bank credit
« vue Salarie »   organised by person - THE PAYROLL VIEW,
because the reconciliation is per
employee

Plus a DAY-DETAIL screen, and SEPARATE SCREENS FOR INDUS in
each view.

EXPORTS: .csv, .xls, .pdf, .xml

The guide notes these exist « pour les integrer dans vos
logiciels de paie ». No column specification is published
for any of them - see the Sample File sheet.

A useful screen detail from the guide: a payment line shown in
BLUE means the day has NOT BEEN CONSULTED. That is a built-in
read-tracking mechanism, and a client working the screens
rather than the exports can use it as a work queue.

═══ THE SAME STATEMENT, TWO OPPOSITE PURPOSES ═══
Which purpose applies is decided by ONE FLAG IN A DIFFERENT
FILING: S21.G00.60.004 in the work-stoppage signal, FR-DSN-003.

SUBROGATED  ( S21.G00.60.004 = '01 - oui' )

The fund pays the EMPLOYER. The employer maintains the
employee's salary.
The BPIJ is a REMITTANCE ADVICE: one bank credit typically
covers many employees, and the statement decomposes it.
Without it, the employer has money it cannot allocate and
cannot verify that the benefits it offset against its
top-up were the benefits actually paid.

NOT SUBROGATED  ( S21.G00.60.004 = '02 - non' )

The fund pays the EMPLOYEE. And yet the employer must
still compute a top-up NET OF benefits it never receives
and did not compute.
The BPIJ is where it would discover the amount - but note
that the guide frames the service around SUBROGATED
benefits paid to the employer's account, so whether a
non-subrogated employer sees useful data here is NOT
established. Where it does not, the amount comes from the
employee's own benefit statement.

Either way the engine must hold a benefit amount whose
provenance is EXTERNAL, DATED and sometimes LATE, and must be
able to regularise a prior period when it arrives.

THIS IS THE ORIGIN OF MOST RETROSPECTIVE SICKNESS ADJUSTMENTS IN
FRENCH PAYROLL. FR-DSN-003 records the same point from the
other end.

═══ THE INDUS - THE HALF A BUILD FORGETS ═══
The guide documents searching for INDUS in their own right:
« Rechercher un indu par vue BPIJ » and « Rechercher un indu par
vue », each with its own screens.

An indu is the fund RECLAIMING benefits it overpaid.

For a SUBROGATED employer that means money going back OUT of the
employer's account, for an absence that has already been settled
in payroll - so it requires a payroll regularisation for the
affected period, not just a bank entry.

A build that reads only the payment screens will:

- reconcile every credit correctly, and
- leave every debit unexplained.

Because indus are comparatively rare, this defect survives
testing and appears in production.

Note also, for the export design: the guide documents payments
and indus as SEPARATE SEARCHES, which suggests separate data
rather than a single signed amount column. Until a real export
settles it, do not assume a reclaim can be reconciled as a
negative payment.

═══ RECONCILING - WHY IT DEPENDS ON A FIELD IN ANOTHER FILING ═══
A subrogated employer receives ONE credit covering MANY
employees. The accounting day and the SIRET are what decompose
it.

But how many streams there are depends on FR-DSN-003:

centralising SIRET DECLARED (S21.G00.60.600)
-> the fund pays ONE SIRET for absences at several
establishments. One stream, decomposed by employee.

centralising SIRET NOT declared
-> the fund settles PER ESTABLISHMENT. Several streams,
each reconciled separately.

A per-establishment reconciliation cannot close the first case,
and a single-stream reconciliation cannot close the second. The
design therefore depends on a rubrique in a different filing -
which is why this is usually discovered during the first month's
reconciliation rather than at design.

One further complication that is normal rather than exceptional:
employees are affiliated to the fund of THEIR OWN RESIDENCE, so
a dispersed workforce means payments arriving from MANY CPAMs.
The guide provides searching by affiliating fund for exactly
this reason.
```

## Sheet: `Sample File`

_55 rows x 1 columns._

```text
BPIJ - bordereau de paiement des indemnites journalieres (inbound) — SAMPLE FILE
OMITTED - the export column layout was NOT OBTAINED, and this workbook will not invent one. The gap is specific: the service DOES export, to four formats - .csv, .xls, .pdf and .xml - and the official guide notes that the exports exist so they can be integrated into payroll software. But no column specification is published for any of them. The fields on the spec sheet are derived from the SEARCH CRITERIA AND VIEWS the guide documents, which establishes that the data exist without establishing what the export columns are called, ordered or typed. Fabricating a CSV would produce something that looks exactly like a specification and is wrong in every column heading - and because the guide explicitly invites integration, it would be built against. No official sample exists in FR-compliance/00-official-sources/sample-files/. The first implementation step for this flow is therefore to obtain ONE REAL EXPORT from a live subrogated client, specify against it, and re-version this workbook with what was found.

SAMPLE FILE DELIBERATELY NOT PROVIDED - THE EXPORT LAYOUT WAS NOT
OBTAINED.

WHAT IS MISSING, PRECISELY:

The service DOES export, to FOUR formats:

.csv   .xls   .pdf   .xml

and the official guide notes that the exports exist so they can be
integrated into payroll software - « pour les integrer dans vos
logiciels de paie ».

But NO COLUMN SPECIFICATION IS PUBLISHED for any of them.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, AND HOW:

The fields on the spec sheet are derived from the SEARCH CRITERIA
and the VIEWS the guide documents - by affiliating fund, by SIRET
and dates, by employee, by accounting day, in a 'vue BPIJ' and a
'vue Salarie', with separate screens for indus. That establishes
that the data EXIST. It does not establish what the export columns
are called, in what order they appear, or how amounts and dates
are formatted.

WHY NOTHING IS INVENTED:

A fabricated CSV would look exactly like a specification and be
wrong in every column heading. And because the guide explicitly
invites integration, it WOULD be built against.

THE FIRST IMPLEMENTATION STEP FOR THIS FLOW:

1. obtain ONE REAL EXPORT, in the chosen format, from a live
subrogated client;
2. specify against it - column names, order, types, how indus are
distinguished from payments, whether the employee is identified
by name or by social security number;
3. re-version this workbook with what was found.

Prefer .csv or .xml over .pdf, and prefer either over reading the
screens - the screens are a consultation interface and change
without notice.

A DATING CAVEAT:

The principal guide obtained is dated JANUARY 2020. The service is
long-established and its structure is stable, but screen details
and export options may have moved since. The 2-day availability
and 33-month retention figures are from that guide; a second
fund's note in the same pack gives 3 to 4 days for its own
population, so the delay varies by fund.
```

## Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

_35 rows x 3 columns._

**Prelevement a la source de l'impot sur le revenu (PAS) - outbound leg — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY**

**How French payroll withholds income tax, and - the point that distinguishes it from every neighbouring system - the fact that the employer never computes the rate. The administration sends a rate, payroll applies it unchanged, and the employer learns nothing about the employee's circumstances. This sheet also separates the two withholdings France operates: the PAS for residents and the art. 182 A retenue a la source for people fiscally domiciled abroad.**

| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
|---|---|---|
| ═══ WHO GETS WITHHELD FROM ═══ |  |  |
| Employees fiscally domiciled in France | YES | The core population. The rate transmitted by the administration is applied to the amount subject to withholding, and the result is declared per employee in S21.G00.50. |
| An employee for whom no rate has ever been received | YES | Withheld at the statutory default grid rate, with the type code identifying which grid. A new hire is in this position by definition: the administration cannot send a rate for someone it does not yet know the employer employs. |
| An employee whose transmitted rate has expired | YES | Also at the default grid. The engine must DATE-CHECK the stored rate on every run - a rate that was valid last month is not self-renewing, and continuing to apply an expired rate is a declared error requiring a S21.G00.56 correction. |
| Company officers treated as employees | YES | Taxed as employees under General Tax Code art. 80 ter and withheld in the same way. |
| Employees fiscally domiciled outside France | YES | But NOT through the PAS. They fall under the retenue a la source of art. 182 A, declared as an individual contribution under code 077. See the dedicated section of the spec sheet - this is the distinction most often collapsed in a payroll build. |
| Apprentices and trainees below the annual exemption threshold | PARTIAL | Their pay up to the annual exemption threshold is not taxable, and the exempt part is carried in the non-taxable-share rubrique S21.G00.50.011. Above the threshold the ordinary mechanism resumes. The threshold is annual, so the exempt share has to be tracked cumulatively across the year and not decided month by month. |
| Self-employed contractors and suppliers | NO | Not employees and not within the employer's withholding obligation. Fees are reported through the S89.G00.32 vehicle, and any withholding on their income is a matter between them and the administration. |
| Pensioners and replacement-income recipients | NO | Their withholding runs through PASRAU, a separate declaration for income other than wages. It is out of scope for this payroll build; the cahier technique for it is held in 00-official-sources/pdfs/ for reference only. |
| ═══ WHAT GETS DECLARED ═══ |  |  |
| The net taxable amount | YES | S21.G00.50.002. Gross less the compulsory social contributions borne by the employee, per the norm's own definition. |
| The amount actually subject to withholding | YES | S21.G00.50.013, declared separately BECAUSE IT CAN DIFFER from the net taxable amount, and required in every case even where the two are equal. |
| The rate applied, its type and its identifier | YES | S21.G00.50.006 to .008. The identifier is the administration's key for reconciling the rate it sent against the rate applied. |
| The amount withheld | YES | S21.G00.50.009, rounded to two decimals under General Tax Code annexe III art. 39 C, 3 f - which the norm cites explicitly. |
| Corrections to a prior month | YES | S21.G00.56, by month of error and type of error. This is the ONLY route: there is no amended income-tax return to file. |
| Third-party garnishment ordered by the tax administration | YES | S21.G00.98, quoting the order identifier the administration sent and reporting how far it could be honoured. |
| The total remitted and the account it is taken from | YES | S21.G00.20, with the affectation entity 'DGFIP_PAS' or 'DGFIP_SATD' and payment by SEPA direct debit. |
| The employee's tax number or household situation | NO | NEVER. The employer holds neither. The whole design of the French scheme is that the employer applies a rate it is given and learns nothing about the employee's circumstances - which is why the employee can opt for a neutral rate without the employer knowing why. |
| The employer's own tax liability | NO | A different obligation entirely. Payroll tax on the employer is FR-DGFIP-003 and is filed on impots.gouv.fr, not here. |
| ═══ TIMING AND RELATIONSHIP ═══ |  |  |
| Declared inside the monthly DSN | YES | There is no separate income-tax filing for payroll. If the DSN is late, the withholding declaration is late with it, and the same single act triggers the payment. |
| Paid by direct debit initiated from the declaration | YES | The employer does not push a payment. The administration debits the account named in S21.G00.20.004, which is why an unregistered or closed account produces an unpaid tax liability from a declaration that was accepted. |
| A quarterly option exists below 11 employees | YES | Where taken, the debit falls on the 18th of the month following the quarter. The DECLARATION stays monthly - only the payment moves. Confusing the two produces three months of apparently unpaid tax. |
| The rate can be applied in the month it is received | NO | It applies from the FOLLOWING payslip. A rate received against the March DSN governs April's payroll. Applying it to March produces a correction against a month already declared. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| An employee who has asked the administration for a neutral rate | YES | The employer sees only a rate and a type code. It does not know, and must not be able to infer, that the employee exercised an option. Any design that surfaces this to a payroll operator defeats the confidentiality the scheme is built on. |
| A short fixed-term contract of two months or less | YES | The norm gives this case its own valorisation rule for the rate identifier. Confirm the client's use of short contracts before configuring, because the ordinary identifier logic does not apply. |
| An overpayment relating to an earlier year | YES | Rate type '99' marks it: no rate applies, because the sum belongs to a tax year already settled between the employee and the administration. |
| Payment delegated to another SIRET | YES | Payment mode '06', and the norm then REQUIRES the remitted amount to be declared as '0.00'. A monitoring rule that alerts on a zero remittance will fire every month for these clients. |
| An 'annule et remplace' declaration with no PAS payment | YES | The norm requires a remittance block to be present with the amount at zero, where the declaration it replaces carried one. Omitting the block is not equivalent to declaring zero. |

Declare the 13 significant characters only - the 2-character control key printed on the card is NOT part of this rubrique.<br><br>Norm definition, CT2026.1.2, quoted verbatim: « Le numéro d'inscription au répertoire (NIR) est l'identifiant unique et invariable des individus inscrits au répertoire national d'identification des personnes physiques (RNIPP). Ce numéro correspond au numéro de sécurité sociale. Ce numéro est composé de 13 chiffres et d'une clé de 2 chiffres. La clé n'est pas à déclarer dans cette rubrique. Cette rubrique permet la déclaration du NIA (numéro d'immatriculation d'attente attribué par les organismes de protection sociale) en l'absence de NIR. Le NIA est constitué comme un NIR dans l'attente d'être certifié (circulaire DSS/sd4c N° 2012-213 du 1er juin 2012). Le Nir doit avoir la forme SAAMMDDCCCNNN avec : S = sexe de la personne physique doit être égal à 1 ou 2 AA = année de naissance de la personne physique doit être comprise entre 00 et 99 MM = mois de naissance de la personne physique doit être compris entre 01 et 12 ou entre 30 et 42 ou entre 50 et 99 ou égal à 20 DD = département de naissance de la personne physique doit être compris entre 01 et 99 ou être égal à 2A ou 2B CCC = commune de naissance de la personne physique doit être comprise entre 001 et 999 NNN = numéro d'inscription la personne physique au registre d'état civil doit être compris entre 001 et 999 ATTENTION : Un NIR ne peut être présent qu'une seule fois dans la déclaration, il doit être unique pour permettre la traçabilité et l'identification de l'individu. Si l'immatriculation est provisoire, ne pas utiliser les numéros provisoires reconnaissables par leur premier caractère égal à 7 ou 8, mais utiliser le NIA qui a été notifié. En l'absence de NIR ou de NIA, il est obligatoire de remplir la rubrique Numéro technique temporaire (S21.G00.30.020). »<br><br>Composite key, 13 characters: position 1 sex (1 male, 2 female), positions 2-3 year of birth, positions 4-5 month of birth, positions 6-7 department of birth, positions 8-10 municipality of birth, positions 11-13 birth sequence number. The 2-digit control key that completes the printed 15-character social security number is NOT declared here. Sourced from the employee's social security card and certified back by the identification return; persists for life, and changes only on a state civil-status correction, which is then carried in the S21.G00.31 change block.<br><br>Composite Key Structure. The NIR is not an opaque number: its 13 significant digits decompose as S(1) sex, 1 male / 2 female - YY(2) year of birth - MM(2) month of birth - DD(2) INSEE department of birth, Corsica coded 2A and 2B and 99 for a birth abroad - CCC(3) INSEE commune code - OOO(3) order number within that commune and month. A 2-digit control key, 97 minus (the 13-digit number modulo 97), is held alongside it for capture validation but is NOT transmitted in this rubrique. Sub-field source: INSEE RNIPP. Persistence: allocated once for life and never reissued. Each base is a separate block occurrence with its own attachment period, which is what allows a correction to be posted to the month it belongs to rather than to the month it is discovered.<br><br>Norm definition, CT2026.1.2, quoted verbatim: « Identifie la règle d'assujettissement par référence aux textes législatifs, réglementaires, conventionnels ou contractuels. Pour plus de précisions sur les éléments de salaires à intégrer dans les bases de cotisations CIBTP se référer au document de référence disponible sur www.cibtp.fr. Pour la base brute de cotisations OPPBTP permanents, indiquez le montant brut sans application du coefficient de majoration. Les valeurs « 36 - CIBTP - Base de cotisations dérogatoire Bâtiment », « 39 - CIBTP - Base de cotisations dérogatoire Travaux Publics » et « 40 - CIBTP - Base de cotisations dérogatoire Partenaires Bâtiment » renvoient aux cotisations pour lesquelles la caisse CIBTP et les organisations professionnelles du BTP ont signé des conventions de mandat pour la perception des cotisations professionnelles. La définition de ces bases est à apporter par les caisses CIBTP. La base IRCANTEC cotisée sert au calcul de l’assiette IRCANTEC pour la période de cotisation et le contrat déclarés. Pour les personnels médicaux hospitaliers relevant de l'IRCANTEC, la base est constitué des émoluments et des indemnités soumis à cotisations IRCANTEC définis par la règlementation. Certaines indemnités peuvent donc ne pas être soumises. Un taux est appliqué à cette base en fonction de l’emploi statutaire du personnel médical hospitalier pour déterminer l’assiette de cotisation. L'assiette caisse de congés spectacles correspond à la rémunération brute acquise par le salarié durant la période de référence, avant toute déduction forfaitaire spécifique pour frais professionnels et toute retenue. En application de l'article D7121-37 du code du travail, les partenaires sociaux d'une branche d'activité ou d'une entreprise peuvent limiter ce montant à un plafond d'indemnité journalière. Pour le régime des pensions civiles et militaires (SRE), la base assujettie est le traitement indiciaire brut éventuellement augmenté de la NBI ou de prime et indemnité. Une attention particulière doit être observée pour les fonctionnaires bénéficiant d'indemnité de sujétion. ## Sheet: `File Structure`

_147 rows x 1 columns._

```text
Prelevement a la source de l'impot sur le revenu (PAS) - outbound leg — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

═══ FILE FORMAT ═══
Norm            : NEODeS, cahier technique CT2026.1.2 (P26V01,
revision 20251224, release 2026.1.0.9).
Physical form   : a flat text file, one rubrique per record. The norm
states the record layout as  [Sxx.Gyy.zz.aaa,'value']
and gives as its own example:
S21.G00.06.001,'332975200'
There is no XML, no XSD and no fixed-width layout.
A build that assumes XML here is wrong.
Field separator : the comma, hex 2C.
Value delimiter : the apostrophe, hex 27, on both sides of the value.
Record delimiter: CR-LF (hex 0D0A) or LF (hex 0A) alone. Both accepted.
Encoding        : ISO/IEC 8859-1 (E), alphabet Latin-1. Named by the norm
as THE usable character table - not UTF-8.
Extension       : .txt (also accepted inside a .zip for bulk deposit).
Record length   : variable, maximum 256 ASCII characters per record.
The per-value length constraint is the rubrique's own,
from its data type.
(cahier technique CT2026.1.2, section 3, p.77)
Declaration     : nature '01 - DSN Mensuelle'
carried in S20.G00.05.001.

═══ STRUCTURAL HIERARCHY ═══
The file is a strict nesting of blocks. A child block may only appear
inside its parent, and the cardinality shown is the norm's own.

S10.G00.00  Envoi                                   {1,1}
S10.G00.01  Emetteur                              {1,1}
S10.G00.02  Contact Emetteur                      {1,1}
S20.G00.05  Declaration                           {1,*}
S21.G00.06  Entreprise                          {1,1}
S21.G00.11  Etablissement                     {1,*}
S21.G00.30  Individu                        {0,*}
S21.G00.40  Contrat                       {1,*}
S21.G00.50  Versement individu          {1,*}
S21.G00.51  Remuneration              {0,*}
S21.G00.78  Base assujettie           {0,*}
S21.G00.81  Cotisation individuelle {0,*}
S21.G00.22  Bordereau de cotisation due     {0,*}
S21.G00.23  Cotisation agregee            {0,*}
S21.G00.20  Versement organisme             {0,*}
S90.G00.90  Total de l'envoi                        {1,1}

The exact block set carried by THIS declaration nature is the one
listed on the spec sheet; blocks the norm forbids for this nature are
shown there as excluded rather than omitted.

═══ TRANSMISSION AND CHANNEL ═══
Channel  : file_upload - a file generated by the payroll software and
deposited on the portal, or sent machine-to-machine via the
same platform's API.
Portal   : net-entreprises.fr, operated by GIP-MDS.
https://www.net-entreprises.fr/
Deposit  : S10.G00.00.007 = '01 - Net-entreprises'. Value '02 - MSA' is
the agricultural channel and is out of scope for this build.
Test mode: S10.G00.00.005 = '01 - envoi fichier test' routes the file
to the test environment. Conformity is proved with the free
self-check tool before going live; there is no product
certification for France (FR-CCG-001 Module 10.4).
Mandate  : a service provider filing on a client's behalf must be
registered on net-entreprises.fr and hold the client's
mandate. That is a registration, not a software approval.

═══ WHERE THE INCOME TAX ACTUALLY LIVES ═══
There is no French income-tax return for payroll. The withholding
is a subset of the monthly DSN, and the payment is a direct debit
the administration initiates from that same declaration.

S21.G00.50  Versement individu
.002  Remuneration nette fiscale       net taxable amount
.006  Taux de PAS                      the rate, as received
.007  Type du taux                     received or which grid
.008  Identifiant du taux              the administration's key
.009  Montant de PAS                   the tax withheld
.011  Part non imposable du revenu     apprentices / trainees
.013  Montant soumis au PAS            ALWAYS declared

S21.G00.56  Regularisation de prelevement a la source
one group PER MONTH corrected - never an aggregate

S21.G00.98  Saisie administrative a tiers detenteur
garnishment ordered by the administration, answered here

S21.G00.20  Versement organisme, with:
.001 = 'DGFIP'          a literal, not a SIRET
.002 = 'DGFIP_PAS' or 'DGFIP_SATD'   (CCH-11)
.010 = '05' or '06'                  (CCH-14)
.005 rounded to the whole euro

═══ THE TWO WITHHOLDING MECHANISMS - v2.8 CHECK B1 ═══
France operates TWO distinct withholdings on employment income.
They are not variants of one another and they are mutually
exclusive for a given person in a given month.

RESIDENT
Levy   : prelevement a la source
Basis  : General Tax Code arts. 204 A to 204 M, art. 1671
Rate   : transmitted by the administration (FR-DGFIP-002), or
the statutory default grid - never computed by the
employer
Carried: S21.G00.50.006 to .013

NON-RESIDENT (fiscally domiciled outside France)
Levy   : retenue a la source
Basis  : General Tax Code art. 182 A
Rate   : the art. 182 A progressive scale - a different scale,
on a differently-computed base, partly liberatory
Carried: S21.G00.81.004, under 'Code de cotisation' = '077',
attached to an assessable base in S21.G00.78

The cahier technique states this at section 2.3.5, in terms, and
gives the equivalent rule for non-employees at S89.G00.92.018 -
where control CCH-11 makes the non-resident withholding permitted
if and only if the PAS amount is absent, and FORBIDDEN otherwise.

Which mechanism applies is decided by the FISCAL residence
rubrique S21.G00.30.022, not by the social-security rubrique
S21.G00.40.024. Section 1.4.1.3 separates the two readings
deliberately: an expatriate can be socially affiliated in France
and fiscally domiciled abroad, or the reverse. Keying tax
treatment off the social-security field is wrong for exactly the
population the field was meant to identify.

═══ THE CALENDAR ═══
One act, two dates: the declaration and the payment.

employer of 50+ paying wages in the same month
DSN deposited      5th of the following month
account debited    8th of the following month

every other employer
DSN deposited     15th of the following month
account debited   18th of the following month

quarterly option, fewer than 11 employees
DSN deposited     monthly, unchanged
account debited   18th of the month after the quarter

Under the quarterly option only the PAYMENT moves. The
declaration stays monthly. Reading the option as a quarterly
declaration produces three months of apparently unfiled tax.

The rate received in a return applies from the FOLLOWING payslip,
not the current one. A rate delivered against the March DSN
governs April's payroll.
```
