## Sheet: `Population Rules`

_22 rows x 5 columns._

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| The rate is received, never computed | S21.G00.50.006, .007, .008 | FR-DGFIP-002 (CRM PAS), or the statutory default grid | The engine stores, per employee, the rate, its type, its identifier and its validity period, as delivered by the tax administration in the return flow. On every run it date-checks the stored rate. If a valid rate is held, it applies it unchanged and re-emits the identifier unchanged. If none is held or the one held has expired, it applies the statutory default grid and sets the type code to the grid actually used - which is territorial, so the employee's place of work decides which grid. At no point does the engine derive a rate from anything it knows about the employee. | A new hire has no transmitted rate by definition and must go to the default grid without anyone intervening. The opposite failure - continuing to apply an expired rate because it is still in the table - is silent, and produces a correction obligation under S21.G00.56 for every month it persisted. |
| The amount subject to withholding is always declared | S21.G00.50.013 | Payroll | The norm states that this amount and the net taxable amount of S21.G00.50.002 may differ, and requires this rubrique to be populated IN ALL CASES, including where the two are equal. It is not conditional on a difference existing. A component that emits it only when it differs from the net taxable amount omits it from the great majority of ordinary payslips and fails on deposit. | Which client-specific elements cause a divergence is a configuration question that must be listed and signed off per client rather than assumed to be empty. |
| The withheld amount and its rounding | S21.G00.50.009 | Payroll | Computed as the amount subject to withholding multiplied by the rate applied, rounded to two decimals. The norm cites the authority explicitly - General Tax Code annexe III, art. 39 C, 3 f - rather than leaving the rounding to the implementer. Round once, at the end, on the product; rounding the rate or the base first produces systematic drift across a large population. | This two-decimal rule is NOT the rule for the remitted total, which is rounded to the whole euro. The two live in the same declaration and a shared rounding helper will get one of them wrong. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| The affectation entity for DGFiP is a fixed literal | S21.G00.20.001 and .002 | Filing component | Control CCH-11 of S21.G00.20: where the social-protection body identifier is the literal 'DGFIP', the affectation entity MUST be 'DGFIP_PAS' or 'DGFIP_SATD'. Note that unlike every other body in this rubrique - which take a SIRET - DGFiP is identified by the literal string. A component that populates a SIRET for the tax administration is rejected. | 'DGFIP_PAS' carries the withholding; 'DGFIP_SATD' carries a third-party garnishment. They are separate remittance blocks even when both fall in the same month, and control CCH-11 of S21.G00.20.014 additionally requires a payment identifier on the garnishment one. |
| The payment mode for DGFiP is constrained | S21.G00.20.010 | Filing component | Control CCH-14: where the body is 'DGFIP', the payment mode must be '05 - prelevement SEPA' or '06 - versement realise par un autre etablissement'. Cheque, transfer and inter-bank payment order are not available for the withholding. Where mode 05 is used, control CCH-12 makes the IBAN mandatory and SIG-13 makes the BIC mandatory. | Where the paying SIRET differs from the establishment's own, SIG-14 forces mode '06' - and the norm then requires the remitted amount to be 0.00. A client with centralised payment therefore declares zero every month, legitimately. |
| The remittance ceiling | S21.G00.20.005 | Filing component | Control CCH-13: where the body is 'DGFIP', the remitted amount must be less than or equal to 999999999.00. This is a real ceiling for very large employers and it is a hard rejection, not a warning. Where an establishment would exceed it, the remittance has to be structured across establishments. | The same rubrique carries a different rounding rule for DGFiP than for other bodies - see the amount format rules below. |
| Non-resident withholding is mutually exclusive with the PAS | S21.G00.81.001 code 077 against S21.G00.50.006 to .013 | Payroll | Cahier technique section 2.3.5: for an employee domiciled outside France, the withholding is declared as an individual contribution with code de cotisation '077', and NOT in the PAS rubriques. The same exclusivity is enforced explicitly for non-employees by control CCH-11 of S89.G00.92.018, which permits the non-resident withholding if and only if the PAS amount is absent, and forbids it otherwise. The two mechanisms cannot both fire for the same person in the same month. | The commonest defect is treating an expatriate as a resident with a default-grid rate. That produces a PAS declaration for someone outside the PAS, an art. 182 A liability that is never declared, and an employee taxed twice on reconciliation. |
| ═══ AMOUNT FORMAT RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Two different rounding rules in one declaration | S21.G00.50.009 against S21.G00.20.005 | Payroll | Per employee, the withheld amount is carried at TWO REAL DECIMALS under General Tax Code annexe III art. 39 C, 3 f. The REMITTED total is, in the norm's own words for DGFiP, 'montant, arrondi a l'entier le plus proche (les deux decimales etant valorisees a zero)' - rounded to the nearest whole euro with the decimals written as zeroes. The field format is two decimals in both cases; the VALUES obey different rules. | The consequence is that the remittance is not the exact sum of the per-employee amounts. A reconciliation control that expects equality reports a false difference of up to fifty centimes every month, and teams then 'fix' the per-employee amounts to make it balance - which is the actual error. |
| Rates | S21.G00.50.006 and S21.G00.56.005, .006 | Payroll | A percentage with two decimals, per the norm's own pattern in column J. The correction rubrique S21.G00.56.005 carries the DIFFERENCE between the rate that should have been applied and the rate actually applied, not the corrected rate - so it is signed, and it is not interchangeable with S21.G00.56.006, which carries the rate as originally declared. | Sending the corrected rate where the difference is expected produces a correction of the wrong magnitude that is nonetheless structurally valid, so it is accepted and settles wrongly. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Correcting a prior month | S21.G00.56.001 to .015 | Payroll | There is no amended income-tax return. A withholding error is corrected inside a later monthly DSN by declaring the month of the error, the type of error, and the deltas. The norm requires ONE CORRECTION GROUP PER MONTH AFFECTED - it states in terms that where an error was repeated over several months, each month must appear. A single aggregate correction covering a range of months is wrong however arithmetically correct its total. | The four error types are not interchangeable: a rate error and a net-taxable-amount error carry different rubrique sets, and the overpayment type has its own. Engines that classify every correction as a net-taxable-amount rectification produce filings the administration accepts and settles against the wrong year. |
| Third-party garnishment | S21.G00.98.001 to .004 | Tax administration order, then payroll | The tax administration sends a garnishment order (saisie administrative a tiers detenteur) with an identifier. Payroll deducts what it can from the employee's pay within the protected minimum, and reports back through this block: the order identifier as received, how far the order could be honoured using the norm's six-value status code, and the amount actually seized. The order identifier must be echoed exactly - it is the administration's key to matching the response to the order. | The status codes distinguish partial from total settlement AND whether the deduction competed with other claims on the same pay. Reporting 'positive with total settlement' where another creditor was in fact competing misstates the priority position, and the public accountant relies on it. |
| The non-resident base | S21.G00.78.001 and .004 with S21.G00.81 | Payroll | The art. 182 A withholding is declared as an individual contribution attached to an assessable base. The base carries its own code from the S21.G00.78.001 list, and the withheld amount goes in S21.G00.81.004 under code de cotisation '077'. The scale is the art. 182 A scale, which is progressive by band and partly liberatory - it is not the PAS rate and it is not a flat rate. | This population is small in most clients and therefore rarely tested. Confirm at implementation whether the client has any employees fiscally domiciled outside France; if the answer is no today, the configuration must still fail loudly rather than silently apply a PAS rate on the day the first one is hired. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Bidirectional constraint | S21.G00.50.007 (rate type) <-> S21.G00.50.008 (rate identifier) | Payroll | The rate identifier is the one carried by the CRM PAS. Where the rate type is '01 - taux transmis par la DGFiP' the identifier belongs to a rate the administration actually sent, and must be echoed unchanged; where a default grid was used there is no administration-issued rate to identify, and the norm gives a specific valorisation for short fixed-term contracts. Each rubrique names the other in its Conditional Reason. | Echoing a stale identifier alongside a default-grid rate tells the administration a rate it sent was applied when it was not, and the divergence surfaces at the employee's annual reconciliation rather than at deposit. |
| Bidirectional constraint | S21.G00.30.022 (fiscal status abroad) <-> S21.G00.81.001 code 077 | HR and payroll | The fiscal-status rubrique is what places an individual outside the PAS and inside art. 182 A. Where it marks work abroad, the withholding belongs under code 077 and the PAS rubriques must not carry an amount. Note that S21.G00.40.024 answers a DIFFERENT question - the social security reading of the same situation - and the cahier technique separates them deliberately at section 1.4.1.3. One cannot be derived from the other. | An expatriate can be socially affiliated in France while fiscally domiciled abroad, or the reverse. A build that keys tax treatment off the social-security rubrique will be wrong for exactly the population it was meant to handle. |
| Bidirectional constraint | S21.G00.56.002 (error type) <-> S21.G00.56.003 to .015 | Payroll | The error type governs which correction rubriques may be populated: a rate error requires the rate as declared and the base as declared in the month of the error; a net-taxable-amount error requires the delta on that amount. Each correction rubrique names the error type in its Conditional Reason and the error type carries the back-references. | Populating a correction rubrique that does not belong to the declared error type is a structural error; populating the right rubrique under the wrong type is not, and is therefore the failure that survives testing. |
| Bidirectional constraint | S21.G00.20.002 (affectation entity) <-> S21.G00.20.014 (payment id) | Filing component | Control CCH-11 of S21.G00.20.014: where the affectation entity is 'DGFIP_SATD', the payment identifier is mandatory. A garnishment remittance without it cannot be matched to the order it settles. | A withholding remittance ('DGFIP_PAS') does not need it, so a component that shares one code path for both remittance types will omit it on the case that requires it. |

**Prelevement a la source de l'impot sur le revenu (PAS) - outbound leg — EXAMPLE FILE ANALYSIS**

| Raw Value | Field Name | Interpretation | Notes |

| ═══ THE RATE, AS RECEIVED AND APPLIED ═══ |  |  |  |
| S21.G00.50.007,'01' | Type du taux de prelevement a la source (S21.G00.50.007) | '01 - Taux transmis par la DGFIP'. A real rate was received for this employee and is being applied. | Any other value means a default grid was used - and which grid is territorial. A single hard-coded default is wrong for a client with overseas-department staff. |
| S21.G00.50.006,'11.50' | Taux de prelevement a la source (S21.G00.50.006) | 11.50 %. Applied exactly as received. | ILLUSTRATIVE value. The employer neither computes nor adjusts it, and does not know why it is what it is. |
| S21.G00.50.008,'2026030112345678' | Identifiant du taux (S21.G00.50.008) | The identifier carried by the CRM PAS that delivered this rate. | ILLUSTRATIVE value. Echoed unchanged - it is the administration's key for reconciling what it sent against what was applied. |
| ═══ THE TWO BASES, WHICH ARE NOT THE SAME NUMBER ═══ |  |  |  |
| S21.G00.50.002,'2650.00' | Remuneration nette fiscale (S21.G00.50.002) | Net taxable pay: gross less the compulsory employee social contributions. | This is the figure that also feeds the employee's pre-filled income-tax return. |
| S21.G00.50.013,'2650.00' | Montant soumis au PAS (S21.G00.50.013) | The amount actually subject to withholding. Equal to the net taxable amount in this simple case - but declared anyway. | The norm requires this rubrique IN ALL CASES. Omitting it when it equals the net taxable amount is the commonest defect on this block, and it fails on ordinary payslips, not edge cases. |
| S21.G00.50.009,'304.75' | Montant de prelevement a la source (S21.G00.50.009) | 2650.00 x 11.50 % = 304.75, rounded to two decimals under General Tax Code annexe III art. 39 C, 3 f. | Round once, on the product. Rounding the rate or the base first drifts across a large population. |
| ═══ NON-RESIDENT TREATMENT - A DIFFERENT LEVY ENTIRELY ═══ |  |  |  |
| S21.G00.30.022,'02' | Statut a l'etranger au sens fiscal (S21.G00.30.022) | '02 - travail a l'etranger'. This individual is outside the PAS. | The FISCAL reading. S21.G00.40.024 answers the separate SOCIAL SECURITY question and may say something different for the same person. |
| S21.G00.81.001,'077' | Code de cotisation (S21.G00.81.001) | '077 - Montant de la retenue a la source effectuee sur les salaires verses aux personnes domiciliees hors de France'. The art. 182 A withholding. | Cahier technique section 2.3.5 states this in terms. For this employee the S21.G00.50 PAS rubriques carry no withholding - the two mechanisms are mutually exclusive. |
| S21.G00.81.004,'420.00' | Montant de cotisation (S21.G00.81.004) | The art. 182 A retenue a la source for the month. | ILLUSTRATIVE value. Computed on the art. 182 A progressive scale, which is not the PAS rate and is not flat. |
| ═══ CORRECTING A PRIOR MONTH ═══ |  |  |  |
| S21.G00.56.001,'012026' | Mois de l'erreur (S21.G00.56.001) | The error occurred in January 2026, and is being corrected in a later month's declaration. | One correction group PER MONTH affected. An error repeated over three months produces three groups, not one aggregate. |
| S21.G00.56.002,'02' | Type d'erreur (S21.G00.56.002) | '02 - Rectification sur taux'. The wrong rate was applied. | The type governs which of the correction rubriques may be populated. Misclassifying the error produces a valid filing that settles wrongly. |
| S21.G00.56.005,'-1.20' | Regularisation du taux (S21.G00.56.005) | The DIFFERENCE between the rate that should have applied and the rate applied - not the corrected rate. | ILLUSTRATIVE value. Sending the corrected rate here is accepted structurally and corrects by the wrong magnitude. |
| ═══ REMITTING THE MONEY ═══ |  |  |  |
| S21.G00.20.001,'DGFIP' | Identifiant Organisme de Protection Sociale (S21.G00.20.001) | The literal string 'DGFIP'. Every other body in this rubrique is identified by a SIRET; the tax administration is not. | A component that formats a SIRET here is rejected. |
| S21.G00.20.002,'DGFIP_PAS' | Entite d'affectation des operations (S21.G00.20.002) | Control CCH-11 admits only 'DGFIP_PAS' or 'DGFIP_SATD' when the body is DGFIP. This block carries the withholding. | A garnishment settlement would be 'DGFIP_SATD' in a SEPARATE block, and would additionally require a payment identifier. |
| S21.G00.20.010,'05' | Mode de paiement (S21.G00.20.010) | '05 - prelevement SEPA'. Control CCH-14 admits only 05 or 06 for DGFiP; the administration debits the employer. | Mode 05 makes the IBAN mandatory (CCH-12) and the BIC mandatory (SIG-13). |
| S21.G00.20.005,'12480.00' | Montant du versement (S21.G00.20.005) | The month's withholding, ROUNDED TO THE NEAREST WHOLE EURO with the decimals written as zeroes - the norm's own DGFiP rule. | ILLUSTRATIVE value. This is NOT the exact sum of the per-employee amounts, which carry two real decimals. Expect a difference of up to fifty centimes and do not 'correct' the per-employee figures to close it. |

L133-5-3 (the DSN and its returns). Technical: cahier technique NEODeS CT2026.1.2 for the consumption rubriques. | Accuracy: HIGH for the consumption side and for the scope determination. The three DSN rubriques in Part B are read from cahier technique CT2026.1.2, including the norm's own statement that the rate identifier in S21.G00.50.008 is 'l'identifiant du taux porte par le CRM PAS ... transmis par la DGFIP' - which is the norm confirming this flow's existence and role. The eight rate-type codes and the territorial grids are the norm's own enumeration, reproduced verbatim. HIGH that this flow is NOT NEOReS: the NEOReS cahier technique 2026.1.0 states 'les comptes rendus PAS sont hors-perimetre de la demarche de normalisation, qui vise les retours de la sphere sociale'. That is a direct quotation and it means a NEOReS parser does not read this return. HIGH for the eleven DGFiP identification controls on the Field Options sheet, quoted from the authority's own control referential (referentiel-unique-des-controles-neores.xlsx, v30/06/2026), where all eleven are recorded as delivered by 'CRM normalise et outil en ligne'. MEDIUM for the return's own structure, which is stated at block level from the platform's service description - envelope information, then declaration information carrying the per-individual rates, the anomaly list and the declaration summary - and is NOT stated at field level. LOW, AND SAID PLAINLY, FOR THE RECORD LAYOUT: it was NOT OBTAINED. It is not in the DSN cahier technique, it is not in NEOReS, and the published note describing it was not retrievable in readable form for this build. Column H records that on every row of Part A instead of carrying invented paths, and sheet 9 carries no fabricated sample. MEDIUM for the two-month rate validity, which comes from the platform's own guidance rather than from a norm, and should be reconfirmed. What would improve it: the CRM PAS specification from DGFiP or GIP-MDS, and one real return retrieved against a live client's DSN. Channel: inbound file retrieval, or API returning XML \| Portal: net-entreprises.fr DSN dashboard \| Source: net-entreprises CRM service description; DSN cahier technique CT2026.1.2 for the consumption rubriques \| CONFIRMED for the channel, LAYOUT NOT OBTAINED |

## Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

_30 rows x 3 columns._

**Compte rendu metier PAS (CRM PAS) - taux de prelevement a la source — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY**

**Where an employee's withholding rate comes from, and what happens when none arrives. This return is the ONLY lawful source of a rate: the employer holds no tax number, asks no question about the employee's household, and computes nothing. Two facts govern the build. THE RATES EXPIRE AFTER TWO MONTHS, so monthly retrieval and a date-check on every payroll run are the only way the mechanism works. And this return is NOT NEOReS - the norm excludes it in terms - so it is a second integration, not a reuse of the first.**

| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
|---|---|---|
| ═══ WHAT THE RETURN DELIVERS ═══ |  |  |
| A withholding rate for each employee | YES | The payload, and the only lawful source of a rate. The employer holds no tax number and asks no question about the employee's household. |
| The identifier of each rate | YES | Echoed back unchanged in the next declaration. The DSN norm defines its own rubrique as 'the identifier of the rate carried by the CRM PAS transmitted by the DGFiP', which is the norm confirming the round trip. |
| The validity of each rate | YES | TWO MONTHS. This is what makes monthly retrieval obligatory rather than advisable, and what makes an expiry check on every payroll run obligatory rather than defensive. |
| Anomalies preventing a rate being issued | YES | Chiefly identification failures - the administration could not match the declared individual. Eleven such controls are catalogued and reproduced on the Field Options sheet. Until they are cleared the employee stays on the default grid. |
| Anomalies on the payment of the withholding | YES | The service description names payment anomalies alongside identification and rate-application ones. |
| Why a particular rate is what it is | NO | NEVER, and this is deliberate. The employer sees a rate and a type code. It does not learn the employee's household situation, and cannot tell whether the employee has exercised the option for a neutral rate. Any design that surfaces an inference about this to a payroll operator defeats the confidentiality the whole scheme rests on. |
| The employee's tax number | NO | The employer never receives one and must never ask for one. |
| Social-sphere anomalies | NO | Those come through FR-URSSAF-002, in a different format. This return is the tax administration's. |
| ═══ WHO MUST ACT ON IT ═══ |  |  |
| The payroll engine, for a rate | YES | Store per employee with the identifier and the validity; apply from the FOLLOWING payslip; date-check on every run; fall back to the statutory grid automatically on expiry. |
| HR master data, for an identification anomaly | YES | The anomaly says the administration could not match the person. The correction belongs in the master record - patching one declaration leaves the anomaly to recur every month and the employee without a rate indefinitely. |
| A payroll operator, deciding whether a rate looks right | NO | There is no such decision. The rate is applied as received. An operator who overrides it is acting outside the scheme, and an engine that permits an override without an audited reason should not. |
| The employee, on being told their rate | NO | The rate appears on the payslip, but the employee's route for changing it is with the tax administration, not with the employer. An employer that accepts rate-change instructions from employees has misunderstood the scheme. |
| ═══ TIMING ═══ |  |  |
| Retrieved every month, without exception | YES | Because the rates expire after two months. A client that retrieves quarterly has, by the third month, a population silently on the default grid. |
| The rate applies from the following payslip | YES | A rate delivered against the March DSN governs April's payroll. Applying it to March means correcting a month already declared, through the S21.G00.56 correction block. |
| A rate applies until it is replaced | NO | It applies until it EXPIRES, which is different. Replacement is the normal case; expiry without replacement is the failure case, and the engine must handle it without human intervention. |
| A missing month can be caught up later | PARTIAL | The rates can be retrieved late, but the payslips already run with the wrong rate cannot be undone - they are corrected in a later monthly DSN through the correction block. So a missed retrieval converts into a correction obligation, not just a delay. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| A new hire | YES | On the default grid by definition, because the administration cannot have sent a rate for somebody it does not yet know the employer employs. The first real rate normally arrives against the first DSN that declares them. |
| An employee the administration cannot identify | YES | Stays on the default grid, and an identification anomaly explains why. The eleven catalogued controls are almost all triggered by hurried onboarding data - placeholder names, placeholder birth dates, an address without a street. |
| An employee working in an overseas department | YES | The default grids are TERRITORIAL. A single hard-coded grid is wrong for these employees, and the error is invisible because the declaration is structurally valid. |
| An overpayment relating to an earlier year | YES | Rate type '99' - no rate applies at all, because the sum belongs to a tax year already settled between the employee and the administration. |
| A short fixed-term contract of two months or less | YES | The norm gives this case its own valorisation rule for the rate identifier. Confirm the client's use of short contracts before configuring. |

## Sheet: `File Structure`

_154 rows x 1 columns._

```text
Compte rendu metier PAS (CRM PAS) - taux de prelevement a la source — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

═══ SCOPE - THIS FLOW IS NOT NEOReS, AND THAT IS A QUOTATION ═══
The NEOReS cahier technique 2026.1.0, in the section defining the
perimeter of normalised organisation returns, states:

« A noter egalement que les comptes rendus PAS sont
hors-perimetre de la demarche de normalisation, qui vise
les retours de la sphere sociale. »

So although this return arrives on the SAME DSN DASHBOARD as the
normalised URSSAF returns specified in FR-URSSAF-002, it is a
DIFFERENT FORMAT. A NEOReS parser does not read it.

Two consequences for planning:

- FR-URSSAF-002 and FR-DGFIP-002 are TWO integrations, not one.
Estimate them separately.

- This is the harder of the two, because NEOReS publishes a
cahier technique, an XSD and a validator, and this flow's
specification is not published in the same way.

The same section of the NEOReS norm names the AT/MP and
bonus-malus rate transmissions as FUTURE candidates for the
normalisation - which is separately useful, because it confirms
that FR-CARSAT-001 is not NEOReS either, today.

═══ STRUCTURE - AT BLOCK LEVEL ONLY, FROM THE SERVICE DESCRIPTION ═══
The platform's own description of how the CRM is built:

INFORMATION ABOUT THE TRANSMISSION
identifiant du flux
version de la norme
SIRET de l'entreprise emettrice

INFORMATION ABOUT THE DECLARATION SUBMITTED
donnees d'identification de la declaration
the withholding RATE of each individual
liste d'anomalies detectees
bilan de la declaration

This is BLOCK level. There is no field-level layout in this
workbook because none was obtained, and column H of Part A says
so on every row rather than carrying an invented path.

Retrieval:
- connect to the net-entreprises space AFTER depositing the
DSN, and collect the return from the dashboard;
- declarants in API mode retrieve it as XML.

═══ THE TWO-MONTH VALIDITY - WHY THIS FLOW CANNOT BE RETRIEVED OCCASIONALLY ═══
The rate applicable to each employee, as carried on the CRM, has
a validity of TWO MONTHS. Collecting the return every month is
therefore not a good practice - it is the only cadence at which
the mechanism works.

What happens when it is not:

month 1   rate received, applied from month 2's payslip
month 2   no retrieval. The month-1 rate is still valid.
month 3   no retrieval. The month-1 rate has now EXPIRED.
The statutory default grid should apply - but an
engine that stored the rate without its expiry
keeps applying it.
month 4+  every payslip is wrong, and every declaration is
structurally perfect.

Nothing chases the employer. The first visible symptom is an
employee's annual reconciliation with the tax administration.

Two controls follow directly, and both belong in the engine
rather than in a procedure:

- a date-check of the stored rate on EVERY payroll run, with
automatic fallback to the correct territorial default grid;
- an alert when a month produces no return for a client or an
establishment.

═══ WHAT THE EMPLOYER NEVER SEES, AND WHY THAT IS DELIBERATE ═══
The employer receives a RATE and a TYPE CODE. It does not
receive, and must not attempt to infer:

- the employee's tax number;
- the employee's household situation or family circumstances;
- whether the employee has exercised the option for a neutral
rate rather than their personal one;
- anything about the employee's other income.

This confidentiality is the design of the scheme, not a policy
overlay on top of it. It is what allowed a withholding system to
be introduced without employers becoming parties to their
employees' tax affairs.

It has concrete design consequences, worth raising at review:

- a screen showing an employee's RATE HISTORY invites
inference from a change;
- a report flagging 'unusual' rates does the same;
- a dashboard of rate distribution by team or grade leaks in
aggregate what cannot be disclosed individually.

None of these is usually built deliberately. They arrive as
well-intentioned features.

It also means the employer CANNOT answer an employee's question
about their rate, and should not try. The employee's route is
their own space with the tax administration. Build the
signposting, not a help desk.

═══ WHY AN EMPLOYEE MIGHT HAVE NO RATE AT ALL ═══
The administration can only send a rate for somebody it has
recognised. Where it cannot, it sends an anomaly instead, and
the employee stays on the default grid until the anomaly is
cleared.

The authority's own control referential
(referentiel-unique-des-controles-neores.xlsx, v30/06/2026)
catalogues ELEVEN DGFiP controls, ALL of them identification
failures, and all delivered as 'CRM normalise et outil en ligne'.
They are reproduced verbatim on the Field Options sheet.

Read as a group they are a map of one failure mode: PLACEHOLDER
DATA ENTERED AT ONBOARDING.

ETC01   family name = 'SN'
ETC02   first name  = 'SP'
ETC03   day of birth   = '99' or '00'
ETC04   month of birth = '99' or '00'
ETC05   birthplace  = 'SLN'
ADR02   address in France with no street

and a second, subtler one: CIVIL-STATUS MISMATCH.

NIR01   the first four letters of the declared family name
match neither the birth name nor the used name held
for the declared social security number
NIR02   no social security number, and no successful match
on civil status either
ADR05   locality not known to the DGFiP
ADR06   street not known to the DGFiP
ETC08   birthplace not known to the DGFiP

The fix for every one of them is UPSTREAM, in the data captured
at hire (FR-URSSAF-001), and in the HR MASTER RECORD - not in
the declaration. Correcting a single month's declaration leaves
the anomaly to recur, and the employee on the default grid
indefinitely.

Note the timing recorded for these controls: the anomaly is
returned to the declarant within a maximum of five days
following the deposit for the address controls, and for the
civil-status ones only where the identification could not be
made at all.
```

## Sheet: `Population Rules`

_23 rows x 5 columns._

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Retrieve every month, per client, and never skip | The whole return | net-entreprises.fr DSN dashboard, or API | The return is made available after the DSN is deposited and must be collected. The rates it carries are VALID FOR TWO MONTHS. Monthly retrieval is therefore not a good practice - it is the only cadence at which the flow works, and a client retrieving less often will have an expiring population it cannot see. Build retrieval as a scheduled step of the payroll cycle, per client and per establishment, with an alert when a month produces no return. | The failure is silent in both directions: nothing chases the employer for not retrieving, and the payslips produced from expired rates look entirely normal. The first visible symptom is an employee's annual reconciliation. |
| Apply the rate unchanged, from the FOLLOWING payslip | S21.G00.50.006 | The return | The rate is applied exactly as received. It governs the payroll AFTER the one whose declaration prompted the return - a rate delivered against the March DSN governs April. There is no adjustment, no smoothing and no override: the employer's role is arithmetic, not judgement. | Applying a newly-received rate to the month just declared produces a correction against a month already filed, which then has to be reported through the S21.G00.56 correction block with the right error type. Two errors from one well-meaning mistake. |
| Date-check the stored rate on EVERY run | The validity | Payroll engine | A rate is not a durable attribute of an employee. Store it with its expiry and test that expiry on every payroll run. Where it has lapsed and no replacement has arrived, fall back to the statutory default grid AUTOMATICALLY and set the type code to the grid actually used. Do not require a human to notice. | This is the single most likely silent defect in a French income-tax implementation. An engine that stores a rate without an expiry applies it for ever, produces perfectly valid declarations, and is wrong from the third month onward for every employee whose rate stopped being refreshed. |
| Echo the identifier unchanged | S21.G00.50.008 | The return | The DSN norm defines this rubrique as the identifier of the rate CARRIED BY THE CRM PAS transmitted by the DGFiP. It is the administration's reconciliation key: it is how the administration confirms that the rate it sent is the rate that was applied. Store it with the rate and re-emit it verbatim. | Echoing a stale identifier alongside a default-grid rate tells the administration that a rate it issued was applied when it was not. The divergence surfaces at the employee's annual reconciliation, long after the payroll team has moved on. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| This is NOT a NEOReS return - a NEOReS parser will not read it | The whole return | Filing component | The NEOReS cahier technique 2026.1.0 states, in its own scope section, that 'les comptes rendus PAS sont hors-perimetre de la demarche de normalisation, qui vise les retours de la sphere sociale'. So although this return arrives on the same DSN dashboard as the normalised URSSAF returns of FR-URSSAF-002, it is a different format. A build that implements the NEOReS parser and assumes it covers the rate return has implemented nothing for the income tax. | Practical consequence for planning: FR-URSSAF-002 and FR-DGFIP-002 are two integrations, not one, and this one is the harder of the two because its specification is not published in the same way. Estimate them separately. |
| Identification anomalies must be fixed in the MASTER RECORD | The anomaly list | HR master data | The eleven catalogued DGFiP controls are all failures to recognise the individual: a family name of 'SN', a first name of 'SP', a birth day or month of '99' or '00', a birthplace of 'SLN', an address with no street, a locality or street the administration does not know, a social security number whose first four name letters do not match, or no number and no successful civil-status match. Every one is a data-quality failure at onboarding. Correct the HR master record; correcting one declaration leaves the employee without a rate for ever. | Note what these controls tell you about the failure mode: 'SN', 'SP' and 'SLN' are placeholder values somebody typed to get past a mandatory field. The fix is upstream, at hire (FR-URSSAF-001), and the cheapest possible point to make it. |
| The default grid is territorial and is not a choice | S21.G00.50.007 | Payroll configuration | The norm's own type-code list carries six default-grid codes: a monthly and a mathematical grid for metropolitan France, the same pair for Guadeloupe, Reunion and Martinique, and the same pair for Guyane and Mayotte. The type code declared must be the grid ACTUALLY USED. And the grid is not optional: an employer cannot elect to keep applying a lapsed rate because it looks more accurate, and cannot ask the employee what to apply instead. | A single hard-coded metropolitan grid is wrong for any client with overseas-department staff, and the error is invisible - the declaration is structurally perfect and the tax is simply the wrong amount. The grids also change with each Finance Act, so refreshing them is an annual scheduled task. |
| Apply returns in production order, not retrieval order | The declaration identification data | Filing component | A correcting or replacing declaration produces its own return. Where several are retrieved together - after an outage, or when a backlog is cleared - applying an older one after a newer one re-applies superseded rates. Order by the return's own production information, not by when it was downloaded. | The same discipline is required for FR-URSSAF-002 and for the same reason. It is worth building once, in the shared retrieval layer, rather than twice. |
| ═══ AMOUNT FORMAT RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| The rate on the DSN side | S21.G00.50.006 | Payroll | A percentage carried with two decimals, per the norm's own pattern in column J of Part B. The withholding computed from it is rounded to two decimals under General Tax Code annexe III art. 39 C, 3 f, which the norm cites explicitly - round once, at the end, on the product of base and rate. | Rounding the rate itself before applying it, or rounding the base first, produces systematic drift across a large population. The norm's citation of the article is a signal that the rounding is prescribed rather than left to the implementer. |
| The return's own formats | Part A of the spec sheet | n/a | NOT SPECIFIED, because the record layout was not obtained. Column J of Part A says so rather than carrying a guess. What is known is that declarants in API mode retrieve the return as XML. | This is the honest limit of this workbook. Everything on the CONSUMPTION side - Part B - is exact, because the DSN norm defines those rubriques precisely. Everything on the RETURN side is stated at block level only. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| The employer computes nothing and asks nothing | The whole flow | The tax administration | This is the structural fact that distinguishes French income-tax payroll from every neighbouring system, and it should be designed for deliberately. The employer holds no tax number, collects no declaration of household circumstances, and derives no rate. It receives a rate, applies it, and reports what it withheld. Any screen, field or process that invites a payroll operator to reason about an employee's tax position is wrong by construction. | It follows that the employee's questions about their rate cannot be answered by the employer, and should not be. The employee's route is their own space with the tax administration. Build the signposting rather than a help desk. |
| Confidentiality is part of the design, not a policy overlay | S21.G00.50.006 and .007 | Payroll engine design | An employee may obtain a neutral rate from the administration without the employer knowing they have done so. The employer sees only a rate and a type code. A system that lets an operator infer the employee's situation - by displaying a rate history, by flagging 'unusual' rates, by reporting rate distributions by team - leaks precisely what the scheme was built to protect. | Worth raising explicitly at design review. The leak is rarely deliberate; it comes from a well-intentioned dashboard. |
| One retrieval process, two formats | FR-URSSAF-002 and this flow | Filing component | Both returns arrive on the same DSN dashboard against the same deposit, and both must be retrieved every month per establishment. But one is NEOReS XML with a published XSD and the other is not NEOReS at all. Build ONE retrieval and scheduling layer, with TWO parsers behind it, and route on what the return actually is rather than on where it came from. | Sharing the retrieval layer also means the outage-and-backlog handling, the per-establishment iteration and the production-order rule are implemented once. |
| Missed retrieval converts into a correction obligation | S21.G00.56 | Payroll | Payslips already run at the wrong rate cannot be unwound. They are corrected in a later monthly DSN through the correction block, with one correction group PER MONTH affected and the correct error type - a rate error, not a net-taxable-amount error. See FR-DGFIP-001. | This is why the retrieval alert matters more than it looks: the cost of a missed month is not a delay, it is a correction for every affected employee for every month it persisted. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Bidirectional constraint | The returned rate <-> S21.G00.50.006 / .007 / .008 | Payroll | The three DSN rubriques are the consumption target of this return and are only meaningful together: the rate, where it came from, and which issued rate it is. Part B of the spec sheet specifies all three from the norm, and each names the others in its Conditional Reason. | The type code is the audit trail. If it says '01 - taux transmis par la DGFIP' then a rate was received and the identifier must be present; if it names a grid, no identifier from the administration exists to echo. |
| Bidirectional constraint | The rate validity <-> the statutory default grid | Payroll engine | The default grid applies precisely where no valid rate is held - either none was ever received, or the one held has expired. The validity is therefore what selects between the two, and each names the other in its Conditional Reason. | The relationship must be evaluated on every run rather than at the moment a rate arrives, because expiry happens by the passage of time and nothing arrives to announce it. |
| Bidirectional constraint | An identification anomaly <-> the absence of a rate | HR and payroll | An identification anomaly is the REASON no rate was issued for that employee. The two are two views of one fact: the administration could not match the person, so it has nothing to send. Reading them separately produces a payroll team puzzled by a permanent default-grid population and an HR team with an anomaly list nobody has connected to it. | Route them to the same place, or at least report them together. The employee on the default grid for eight months and the anomaly listed for eight months are the same person. |

## Sheet: `Sample File`

_52 rows x 1 columns._

```text
Compte rendu metier PAS (CRM PAS) - taux de prelevement a la source — SAMPLE FILE
OMITTED - the CRM PAS record layout was NOT OBTAINED for this build, and this workbook will not invent one. The gap is specific and is worth stating precisely: the layout is not in the DSN cahier technique CT2026.1.2, it is not in the NEOReS norm (which expressly excludes the PAS returns from its scope), and the published note describing the comptes rendus metier for the PAS was not retrievable in readable form. No official sample exists in FR-compliance/00-official-sources/sample-files/. Fabricating a return for a flow whose only consumer is a parser would guarantee that the parser was built to this workbook's guesses. What IS specified exactly, because the DSN norm defines it exactly, is the CONSUMPTION side: Part B of the spec sheet carries the three rubriques the returned values feed, with the norm's own formats, patterns and code lists, and the Field Options sheet carries the eight rate-type codes and the eleven DGFiP identification controls verbatim. That is enough to build the payroll behaviour correctly; it is not enough to build the parser, and the difference is stated rather than blurred.

SAMPLE FILE DELIBERATELY NOT PROVIDED - THE LAYOUT WAS NOT OBTAINED.

WHAT IS MISSING, PRECISELY:

The CRM PAS record layout. It is:
- NOT in the DSN cahier technique CT2026.1.2, which specifies the
OUTBOUND declaration and only references the CRM PAS as the
source of the rate identifier;
- NOT in NEOReS 2026.1.0, which states in its own scope section
that 'les comptes rendus PAS sont hors-perimetre de la demarche
de normalisation, qui vise les retours de la sphere sociale';
- published in a note on the comptes rendus metier for the PAS
which was not retrievable in readable form for this build.

WHAT IS KNOWN ABOUT THE FILE:

- declarants in API mode retrieve the CRM in XML;
- it is made available on the DSN dashboard after the DSN is
deposited, and is retrieved from there;
- it is structured as information about the TRANSMISSION - flow
identifier, norm version, sending company SIRET - followed by
information about the DECLARATION submitted: its identification
data, the withholding rate of each individual, the list of
anomalies detected, and the summary of the declaration;
- the rates it carries are VALID FOR TWO MONTHS.

WHY NOTHING IS INVENTED:

This return has exactly one consumer: a parser. A fabricated
instance would be used to build that parser and would encode this
workbook's guesses about element names and nesting as though they
were the specification. That is a C25 audit failure with a direct
operational consequence.

WHAT IS SPECIFIED EXACTLY INSTEAD:

The CONSUMPTION side. Part B of the spec sheet carries the three
DSN rubriques the returned values feed - S21.G00.50.006, .007 and
.008 - with the norm's own lengths, formats, patterns and control
rules. The Field Options sheet carries the eight rate-type codes
and the eleven DGFiP identification controls verbatim.

That is enough to build the PAYROLL BEHAVIOUR correctly. It is not
enough to build the PARSER.

TO CLOSE THIS GAP:
request the CRM PAS specification from GIP-MDS or DGFiP, or
retrieve a real return against a live client's DSN deposit. Then
replace Part A of the spec sheet and this sheet, and re-version.
```

## Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

_27 rows x 3 columns._

**Taxe sur les salaires - releve de versement provisionnel 2501-SD et declaration annuelle 2502-SD — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY**

**Who pays the French payroll tax, how it is computed, and where it is filed. Three things distinguish it from everything else in this set. It is an EMPLOYER tax on its own payroll, not a withholding from employees - it is not FR-DGFIP-001. It is filed on impots.gouv.fr, NOT on net-entreprises.fr, and is the only France filing outside the DSN platform. And its incidence follows the employer's VAT position rather than its payroll, which is why line 12 code H - the taxable percentage - is an accounting figure that payroll must be given and cannot derive.**

| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
|---|---|---|
| ═══ WHO PAYS IT ═══ |  |  |
| An employer not subject to VAT, or subject on less than 90 % of turnover | YES | The general test in CGI art. 231. In practice: banks, insurers, health and social bodies, associations, professional bodies, and holding companies with little or no taxable turnover. |
| An employer subject to VAT on all its turnover | NO | Outside the tax. Most commercial employers are in this position, which is why the payroll tax is invisible in most French payroll builds and then arrives as a surprise on the first liable client. |
| An employer partially subject to VAT | PARTIAL | Liable on a PROPORTION, entered at line 12 code H of form 2502-SD. The proportion is an accounting determination made by the client's finance function from its turnover - payroll neither holds it nor can compute it, and a proportion carried unchanged from a prior year is the commonest cause of a materially wrong figure. |
| An employer whose annual tax does not exceed EUR 1,200 | NO | The franchise. And the notice adds that where no payment is due because of the reliefs - the franchise, or the art. 1679 A abatement - the employer is EXEMPT FROM FILING the 2501-SD slips and the 2502-SD return at all. Relief here removes the filing, not just the payment. |
| An employer within CGI art. 1679 A | PARTIAL | Associations under the 1901 Act, public-interest foundations, cancer-treatment centres, trade unions and their unions, mutual societies in the stated circumstances, and their groupings. Liable, but with a large abatement that removes the tax entirely for most small ones. |
| ═══ WHAT IS TAXED ═══ |  |  |
| Gross remuneration paid to employees | YES | The base is broadly the social security base. The normal rate applies to the TOTALITY of each individual's gross remuneration; the increased rates are additional bands on top of it, not alternatives to it. |
| Remuneration in the overseas departments | YES | At reduced rates - 2.95 % in Guadeloupe, Martinique and Reunion, 2.55 % in Guyane and Mayotte - and WITHOUT the increased rates, which the notice states do not apply there. A client with staff on both sides needs two banding regimes. |
| The third increased rate | NO | ABOLISHED for remuneration paid from 1 January 2018 by art. 90 of the Finance Act for 2018, and the notice says so expressly. A configuration carried over from before then must be checked for a third band that no longer exists. |
| The employer's own contributions and the withholding | NO | This tax is computed on remuneration, not on other taxes. It has nothing to do with FR-DGFIP-001, the withholding of employees' income tax, beyond sharing an authority. |
| ═══ TIMING AND RELATIONSHIP ═══ |  |  |
| The periodicity is set by LAST year's liability | YES | And fixed for the whole year. Below EUR 4,000 annual only; EUR 4,000 to EUR 10,000 quarterly; above EUR 10,000 monthly. A client that grows across a threshold changes periodicity NEXT year, not this one. |
| An instalment is paid for the last period of the year | NO | Expressly not. The notice states that no payment is made and no slip filed for the last quarter or last month of the year - that payment is included with the annual return. A build that files twelve slips a year files one too many. |
| The base is also declared in the DSN | YES | Monthly per employee under S21.G00.79.001 code 91, and annually per establishment under S21.G00.44.001 codes 009, 010, 015 and 016. The notice states that this does NOT remove the obligation to file the 2501-SD and 2502-SD in the ordinary way. |
| A company with several establishments files one return | YES | The notice is explicit: a company with several establishments pays ONE SINGLE GLOBAL AMOUNT for all of them. Note the asymmetry with the DSN, where the annual base is declared PER ESTABLISHMENT. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| Transfer or cessation of business | YES | The annual return is due within 60 days and at the latest by 15 January of the following year, with the payment. |
| Death of the employer | YES | Within six months of the death and at the latest by 15 January of the following year. |
| A part-year of activity | YES | But the EUR 1,200 franchise limit is appreciated WHATEVER THE LENGTH of the period of activity - the notice says so. It is not prorated, which is favourable to a business that started late in the year. |
| A multi-sector employer | YES | Form 2502-SD carries columns for a single or first sector, a second sector, a third sector and a total, so each base may be declared up to four times. The sector split is an accounting determination, not a payroll one. |
| An employer with a Treasury claim | YES | May pay by set-off, ticking the box on the form face and filing form 3516 - except where the set-off is a carry-forward onto the following year's payroll-tax instalments, for which the form states 3516 is not to be filed. |

## Sheet: `File Structure`

_139 rows x 1 columns._

```text
Taxe sur les salaires - releve de versement provisionnel 2501-SD et declaration annuelle 2502-SD — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

═══ FILE FORMAT AND CHANNEL - v2.7 STEP 3.5, VERIFIED ═══
This is the ONLY filing in the France set that does not go through
net-entreprises.fr. Getting the portal right matters: the social
portal and the tax portal are different portals with different
credentials, and labelling a tax filing with the social portal is
the specific failure v2.7 STEP 3.5 exists to prevent.

Channel   : online_form (portal form), with an EDI route
available through an accounting provider
Portal    : impots.gouv.fr, espace abonne professionnel,
service 'payer TS'
Filing    : COMPULSORY electronic, from 1 January 2019
CGI art. 1649 quater B quater, XIV
Payment   : COMPULSORY teleregulement, since 2015
CGI art. 1681 septies, al. 5
Penalty   : CGI art. 1738 - 0,2 % of the amount declared or paid,
minimum EUR 60
Set-off   : possible against a Treasury claim (VAT credit,
corporation-tax excess, payroll-tax excess) by
ticking the box on the form face and filing form
3516 - EXCEPT for a carry-forward onto the following
year's payroll-tax instalments, for which the form
states 3516 is NOT to be filed.

Status    : CONFIRMED for channel, portal and legal basis.
FORMAT TO CONFIRM for the EDI route - neither form
cites a cahier des charges or an XSD, and none was
found. Do not build an EDI interface against an
assumed layout.

═══ FORM 2501-SD - RELEVE DE VERSEMENT PROVISIONNEL, CERFA 11060*18 ═══
A short form. The identification block is pre-printed by the
administration, and the form instructs the filer to strike through
and correct IN RED any pre-printed detail that no longer matches
the company's situation.

header   SIE | Numero de dossier | cle | Periode |
Secteur d'activite | CDI | code service
N° d'identification de l'etablissement (SIRET)

VERSEMENT DE LA TAXE AU TITRE DU MOIS OU DU TRIMESTRE
1     Montant de la taxe due au titre du mois ou du trimestre
2     Excedent de versement resultant du report de l'annee
precedente a imputer (s'il y a lieu)
3     Montant net de la taxe due  ( 1 - 2 )

payment  Date | Somme | Telephone | Adresse electronique |
Signature | Paiement par imputation [ ]

Three declared amounts. That is the whole form. All the difficulty
is in line 1, which is a per-employee banded computation summed to
a company total - see the Population Rules and the Example
Analysis sheets.

═══ FORM 2502-SD - DECLARATION ANNUELLE, CERFA 11824*25 ═══
The form prints a LINE NUMBER and a CODE LETTER against every box,
and both are carried in column D of the spec sheet. Section I also
carries four columns - 'Secteur unique ou 1er secteur', '2e
secteur', '3e secteur' and a total - so each base may be declared
up to four times by a multi-sector employer.

I. LIQUIDATION DE LA TAXE
01  A    Base taux normal - Metropole
02  A1   Base 1er taux majore - Metropole
03  A2   Base 2eme taux majore - Metropole
04  B    Base taux normal (Guadeloupe, Martinique, Reunion)
05  C    Base taux normal (Guyane, Mayotte)
06  D0   A  x 4,25 %
07  D1   A1 x 4,25 %
08  D2   A2 x 9,35 %
09  E    B  x 2,95 %
10  F    C  x 2,55 %
11  G    Lignes D0+D1+D2+E+F
12  H    Pourcentage d'imposition
13  I    Total taxe brute   G x H = I

II. MESURES D'ALLEGEMENT
14  J    Franchise            (line 13 <= 1 200)
15  K    Decote               (1 200 < line 13 <= 2 040)
(2 040 - line 13) x 3/4
16  L    Abattement CGI art. 1679 A
17  M    Taxe nette avant imputation
= ligne 13 - (ligne 14 OU ligne 15 + ligne 16)

III. PAIEMENT OU EXCEDENT
18  N    Acomptes deja verses ou excedents reportes
26  T    Montants deja verses au titre du solde
27  U    Remboursement deja demande
20  P    Solde de la taxe a acquitter
= 17 - 18 - 26 + 27, si > 0
21  Q    Excedent de versement
= 18 - 17 + 26 - 27, si >= 0
22     R  Remboursement demande (joignez un RIB)
22 bis R  Ou demande d'imputation sur echeance future
23     S  Et/ou report annee suivante sur 2501

Two layout traps:

Lines 26 and 27 sit BETWEEN lines 18 and 20 on the form face,
despite their numbers - they were added later. Ordering fields by
line number places them wrongly.

Lines 22 and 22 bis share the code letter R, because they are
alternative destinations for the same excess. A code letter is
not a unique key on this form.

═══ WHERE THIS TAX MEETS THE DSN ═══
The same base is declared twice, to the same authority, by two
routes. Notice 2501 NOT-SD states in terms that the DSN obligation
does NOT remove the obligation to file 2501-SD and 2502-SD.

impots.gouv.fr             net-entreprises.fr (in the DSN)
-----------------------    ----------------------------------
2502-SD line 01 code A     S21.G00.44.001 = '009'  (liable)
S21.G00.79.001 = '91'   (monthly,
per employee)
2502-SD line 02 code A1    S21.G00.44.001 = '015'
2502-SD line 03 code A2    S21.G00.44.001 = '016'
(not liable)               S21.G00.44.001 = '010'

Three asymmetries to design around:

GRANULARITY. The tax form is filed by the COMPANY - the notice
requires one single global payment for all establishments. The
DSN declares the annual base PER ESTABLISHMENT. The
per-establishment figures must sum to the company figure, which
makes a useful control.

ROUNDING. The tax forms are in WHOLE EUROS, bases included. The
DSN carries the same base at TWO DECIMALS. The two legitimately
differ by up to fifty centimes; a reconciliation must tolerate
that and not 'fix' either side.

OWNERSHIP. In most client organisations payroll files the DSN
and finance files the tax forms. Neither sees the other's
figure. Build the reconciliation and give the output to whoever
owns the tax return.
```

## Sheet: `Population Rules`

_23 rows x 5 columns._

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Band per employee, never per company | Lines 01, 02, 03 / A, A1, A2 | Payroll | The normal rate applies to the totality of EACH INDIVIDUAL's gross remuneration; the first increased rate applies to that individual's pay above the lower threshold and up to the upper one; the second applies above the upper threshold. Because the thresholds are per person, a company-level total cannot be banded - the split must be computed employee by employee and then summed. The notice's own worked example demonstrates it across three employees and is reproduced in full on the Example Analysis sheet. | The thresholds have monthly, quarterly and annual expressions and the notice publishes all three. Use the one matching the filing period: applying the annual threshold to a monthly computation produces almost no increased-rate base at all. |
| Round everything to the whole euro - including the bases | Every amount on both forms | Payroll | Both forms carry the rule on their face: 'L'arrondissement des bases et des cotisations s'effectue a l'euro le plus proche'. It applies to the BASES as well as to the tax. This is unusual - the DSN carries two decimals almost everywhere - and it is the half most often missed, because a build that rounds only the tax will disagree with the administration's recomputation from the rounded bases. | The notice's own worked examples round only at the end, and print the unrounded intermediate figures. Follow the examples: compute at full precision, round the declared figures. |
| The taxable percentage comes from finance, not payroll | Line 12 / code H | The client's finance function | For an employer wholly outside VAT the percentage is 100. For an employer partially subject to VAT it is the taxable proportion computed from turnover - an accounting determination that payroll does not hold and cannot derive. It must be obtained in writing, for each year, and its revision must be a scheduled task rather than an assumption. | This is the single input that most often makes an arithmetically perfect payroll-tax figure materially wrong, and because it is a multiplier at line 12 the error scales with the whole liability. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| No instalment for the last period of the year | 2501-SD, the final month or quarter | Filing calendar | The notice states it plainly: no payment is to be made and no 2501-SD filed for the last quarter or the last month of the year, because that payment is included in the payment accompanying the annual return. A monthly filer therefore files ELEVEN slips and one annual return, not twelve and one. | A scheduler built on 'file every month' produces a twelfth slip that duplicates part of the annual settlement, and the reconciliation between the two forms then never balances. |
| The franchise and the decote are mutually exclusive | Lines 14 and 15 / codes J and K | Filing component | The form's own line 17 arithmetic encodes it: 'ligne 13 - (ligne 14 OU ligne 15 + ligne 16)'. The franchise applies at or below EUR 1,200; the decote applies above EUR 1,200 and up to EUR 2,040. One or the other, never both. | The decote formula is printed on the form and is (2,040 - line 13) x 3/4. Note that a PROVISIONAL decote may also have been taken during the year on the instalment slips, and the notice states that it is REGULARISED at annual liquidation - so an employer can give some of it back here. |
| The abatement cap changes every year | Line 16 / code L | The client's tax function, and the year's notice | The abatement of CGI art. 1679 A is capped, and the cap is published annually in the notice rather than fixed in the form. The 2502-SD edition for 2025 prints EUR 24,041; notice 2501 NOT-SD gives EUR 24,256 for 2026. A hard-coded cap under-relieves as the figure rises and over-relieves if it ever falls. | The eligibility test is separate from the amount and is a legal determination: the form's footnote enumerates the qualifying bodies. Obtain it in writing from the client's tax function rather than inferring it from the client's legal form. |
| An excess must be given a destination | Line 21 / code Q with lines 22, 22 bis and 23 | Client treasury, then payroll | Where line 21 shows an excess, the form requires it to be carried to line 22 (refund, with bank details attached), line 22 bis (set-off against a future liability, with the page-1 box ticked) or line 23 (carry forward onto next year's instalment slips) - and says 'ET/OU', so it may be split. An excess left without a destination is an incomplete return. | Only line 23 concerns payroll: it is the amount that may later appear at line 2 of a 2501-SD slip in the FOLLOWING year. The engine must therefore carry it across the year boundary, and lines 22 and 22 bis must not be. |
| ═══ AMOUNT FORMAT RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Whole euros throughout, nearest-euro rounding | Every amount on both forms | Filing component | Nearest euro, on bases and on tax alike, per the rule printed on both form faces. There are no decimals anywhere on either form. This differs from the DSN, which carries the SAME BASE at two decimals under S21.G00.79.004 - so the two declarations of one figure legitimately differ by up to fifty centimes and a reconciliation must tolerate that. | The notice's worked examples show the practice: 2,550.40 EUR of computed tax is declared as 2,550. |
| The scale is territorial and the bands are not universal | Lines 01 to 10 | Payroll configuration | Metropolitan France: 4.25 % normal, plus 4.25 % on the first band and 9.35 % on the second. Guadeloupe, Martinique and Reunion: 2.95 %, NO increased rates. Guyane and Mayotte: 2.55 %, NO increased rates. A single company-wide banding routine is therefore wrong for any client with overseas-department staff, and the error is an over-assessment, so nobody complains. | The territorial regimes are mutually exclusive per employee: one person's remuneration belongs to exactly one of lines 01-03, 04 or 05. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Declare the same base twice, from one computation | S21.G00.79.001 code 91 and S21.G00.44.001 codes 009/010/015/016, against 2502-SD lines 01, 02, 03 | Payroll | Notice 2501 NOT-SD requires the payroll-tax base to be declared in the DSN monthly per employee under code 91, and annually per establishment under codes 009, 010, 015 and 016 - and states in terms that this does not remove the obligation to file the 2501-SD and 2502-SD. The same figures therefore travel by two routes to the same authority. They must be produced by ONE computation and reconciled before either is filed. | In most client organisations payroll files the DSN and finance files the tax forms. That makes a divergence easy to create and invisible to both sides until an enquiry. Build the reconciliation and give the output to whoever owns the tax return. |
| Aggregate at company level for the form, per establishment for the DSN | 2501-SD SIRET against S21.G00.44 | Payroll | The notice requires a company with several establishments to pay ONE SINGLE GLOBAL AMOUNT for all of them. But the DSN declares the annual base PER ESTABLISHMENT. The engine therefore needs the same underlying data at two granularities, and the establishment figures must sum to the company figure. | This asymmetry is a useful control in itself: if the per-establishment DSN figures do not sum to the amount filed on impots.gouv.fr, one of the two is wrong. |
| Carry the excess across the year boundary | 2502-SD line 23 code S into 2501-SD line 2 | Payroll and the client's finance function | An excess carried forward on the annual return is what may be set off at line 2 of an instalment slip in the FOLLOWING year. Only an excess shown on the previous year's annual return, and whose refund was not requested, qualifies. The engine must hold it as an opening balance for the new year rather than recompute it. | The other two destinations - refund and set-off against a different liability - do NOT carry into payroll. A build that treats every excess as a carry-forward will set off an amount the client has already been refunded. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Bidirectional constraint | 2502-SD line 14 code J <-> line 15 code K <-> line 17 code M | Filing component | Franchise and decote are alternatives, selected by where line 13 falls against EUR 1,200 and EUR 2,040, and line 17's printed arithmetic - 'ligne 13 - (ligne 14 ou ligne 15 + ligne 16)' - is what enforces the exclusivity. Each of the three rows names the others in its Conditional Reason. | Because the form prints the formula, an electronic filing will usually catch a double claim. A payroll engine that computes the figure for the client will not, unless it is built to. |
| Bidirectional constraint | 2502-SD line 20 code P <-> line 21 code Q | Filing component | The year either owes or is owed. Both are conditional on the sign of the same printed arithmetic over lines 17, 18, 26 and 27, and exactly one of them may be populated. Each names the other. | Lines 26 and 27 exist only where an initial annual return was already filed for the period, and they sit BETWEEN lines 18 and 20 on the form face despite their numbers - a build that orders fields by line number will place them wrongly. |
| Bidirectional constraint | 2502-SD line 21 code Q <-> lines 22, 22 bis and 23 | Client treasury | An excess requires a destination and may be split across them - the form says 'ET/OU'. Note that lines 22 and 22 bis share the printed code letter R, because they are alternative destinations for the same money. | Line 22 requires bank details attached; line 22 bis requires the page-1 checkbox; line 23 is the only one that reaches payroll. |
| Bidirectional constraint | 2502-SD line 23 code S <-> 2501-SD line 2 | Payroll | The carry-forward on the annual return is the source of the set-off on the following year's instalment slips. The two rows reference each other across the two forms and across the year boundary. | This is the only constraint in this workbook that spans two documents and two tax years, which is exactly why it is the one a build forgets. |
| Bidirectional constraint | 2502-SD lines 01-03 <-> line 04 code B <-> line 05 code C | Payroll | The territorial regimes are mutually exclusive per employee. A person's remuneration is metropolitan, or Guadeloupe / Martinique / Reunion, or Guyane / Mayotte. Lines 04 and 05 carry NO increased rates, so an employee who moves between regimes mid-year is banded differently before and after. | Each of the five rows names the others. The mid-year mover is the case that breaks a naive implementation, because the annual thresholds cannot simply be applied to that person's whole year. |

**Taxe sur les salaires - releve de versement provisionnel 2501-SD et declaration annuelle 2502-SD — EXAMPLE FILE ANALYSIS**

| Raw Value | Field Name | Interpretation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| ═══ THE OFFICIAL WORKED EXAMPLE - MONTHLY, THREE EMPLOYEES. REPRODUCED FROM NOTICE 2501 NOT-SD, 2026 EDITION. THESE ARE THE ADMINISTRATION'S OWN FIGURES, NOT INVENTED ONES ═══ |  |  |  |

The notice adds: the remuneration being below 1 535 EUR, there is no 9,35 % increase. Tax: 52,32 EUR. | Note that the normal rate is charged on the WHOLE 1 000, and the increased rate again on the part above 769. The bands are additional, not alternative. |
| Employee 2: 5 000 EUR gross for the month | All three metropolitan bands | 5 000 x 4,25 % = 212,50; (1 535 - 769) x 4,25 % = 32,56; (5 000 - 1 535) x 9,35 % = 323,98. Tax: 569,04 EUR. | The first increased band is capped at the width between the two thresholds - 1 535 less 769 - however high the salary goes. |
| Employee 3: 15 000 EUR gross for the month | All three metropolitan bands | 15 000 x 4,25 % = 637,50; (1 535 - 769) x 4,25 % = 32,56; (15 000 - 1 535) x 9,35 % = 1 258,98. Tax: 1 929,04 EUR. | Same first-band width as employee 2. Only the second band grows. |
| Employer total for the month | 2501-SD line 1 | 52,32 + 569,04 + 1 929,04 = 2 550,40 EUR, ARRONDI A 2 550 EUR. | The notice's own rounding, at the END of the computation and to the nearest whole euro. Declared on line 1 of the instalment slip as 2550. |
| ═══ THE OFFICIAL WORKED EXAMPLE - QUARTERLY. SAME SCALE, QUARTERLY THRESHOLDS ═══ |  |  |  |
| One employee, 15 000 EUR a month = 45 000 EUR for the quarter | Quarterly banding | 45 000 x 4,25 % = 1 912,50; (4 606 - 2 307) x 4,25 % = 97,71; (45 000 - 4 606) x 9,35 % = 3 776,84. Tax: 5 787,05 EUR, arrondi a 5 787 EUR. | The thresholds are the QUARTERLY ones - 2 307 and 4 606, being the annual 9 229 and 18 423 divided by four. Applying the annual thresholds to a quarterly computation would produce almost no increased-rate base. |
| ═══ THE RELIEFS, TESTED IN ORDER ═══ |  |  |  |
| Line 13 code I = 1 100 | Franchise, line 14 code J | At or below EUR 1,200, so the whole gross tax is carried to line 14 and nothing is due. | ILLUSTRATIVE figure. The notice adds that the employer is then exempt from filing the slips and the annual return at all - and that the EUR 1,200 limit is not prorated for a part-year. |
| Line 13 code I = 1 800 | Decote, line 15 code K | Above EUR 1,200 and not above EUR 2,040, so the relief is (2 040 - 1 800) x 3/4 = 180 EUR. | ILLUSTRATIVE figure, real formula - it is printed on the form face. A provisional decote may already have been taken during the year on the instalment slips, and is regularised here. |
| Line 13 code I = 44 603, employer within art. 1679 A | Abatement, line 16 code L | The gross tax less the franchise or decote exceeds the cap, so the cap is carried: EUR 24,041 for 2025 per the form, EUR 24,256 for 2026 per notice 2501 NOT-SD. | THE CAP MOVES EVERY YEAR and is published in the notice, not fixed in the form. Take it from the year's own notice. |
| ═══ THE SAME BASE, DECLARED AGAIN IN THE DSN ═══ |  |  |  |
| S21.G00.79.001,'91' | Type de composant de base assujettie (S21.G00.79.001) | '91 - Base de taxe sur les salaires au taux normal'. Declared for EACH EMPLOYEE, EVERY MONTH, whatever the instalment arrangements. | Quoted requirement from notice 2501 NOT-SD. Even an employer that pays the tax once a year declares this base monthly. |
| S21.G00.44.001,'015' | Code taxe (S21.G00.44.001) | '015 - Assiette de la taxe sur les salaires au premier taux'. The DSN counterpart of line 02 code A1 on form 2502-SD. | Codes 009 liable, 010 not liable, 015 first increased band, 016 second increased band. ## Sheet: `Sample File`

_46 rows x 1 columns._

```text
Taxe sur les salaires - releve de versement provisionnel 2501-SD et declaration annuelle 2502-SD — SAMPLE FILE
OMITTED - and this is a v2.7 STEP 3.5 outcome, not an oversight. The channel for this filing is a PORTAL FORM: compulsory electronic filing on impots.gouv.fr through the espace abonne professionnel, or EDI through an accounting provider. Neither form cites a cahier des charges or an XSD, and none was found; no official sample file exists in FR-compliance/00-official-sources/sample-files/. The build instruction is explicit that where the channel is an online portal form, sheet 9 is omitted or replaced by a statement of the verified channel rather than filled with a fabricated CSV or XML - a fabricated sample is a C25 audit failure. What IS available, and IS reproduced in this workbook, is the FORM ITSELF: every line number and code letter is on the spec sheet, and the administration's own worked examples are on the Example Analysis sheet with their real figures. That is a better artifact than an invented file, because it is what the client's accountant will actually be looking at.

SAMPLE FILE DELIBERATELY NOT PROVIDED - THE CHANNEL IS A PORTAL FORM.

VERIFIED CHANNEL (v2.7 STEP 3.5):

Channel  : online_form, with file_upload available by EDI through an
accounting provider
Portal   : impots.gouv.fr, espace abonne professionnel,
service 'payer TS'
https://www.impots.gouv.fr/
NOT      : net-entreprises.fr. This is the ONLY filing in the France
set that does not go through the DSN platform. The social
portal and the tax portal are different portals.
Source   : the form faces themselves, citing CGI art. 1649 quater B
quater XIV (compulsory electronic filing from 1 January
2019) and art. 1681 septies al. 5 (compulsory electronic
payment since 2015).
Penalty  : CGI art. 1738 - 0,2 % of the amount declared or paid,
minimum EUR 60, for failing to file or pay electronically.
Status   : CONFIRMED for the channel and the portal.
FORMAT TO CONFIRM for the EDI route: no cahier des charges
or XSD is cited on either form, and none was found. Do not
build an EDI channel against an assumed layout - obtain
the specification from the client's accounting provider or
from the DGFiP EDI-TDFC documentation first.

WHY NO SAMPLE IS INVENTED:

A fabricated CSV or XML for a portal-form filing is a C25 audit
failure, and it would be used to build an interface to a channel
that does not accept files in that shape.

WHAT IS PROVIDED INSTEAD, AND IS BETTER:

- the complete form structure, with the REAL printed line numbers
(01 to 27) and code letters (A, A1, A2, B, C, D0, D1, D2, E, F, G,
H, I, J, K, L, M, N, T, U, P, Q, R, S) in column D of the spec
sheet - nothing derived;
- the administration's OWN worked examples, with its own figures and
its own rounding, on the Example Analysis sheet;
- the 2026 scale, thresholds and reliefs on the Field Options sheet.

That is what the client's accountant is looking at, and it is what a
developer needs in order to produce the right numbers.
```
