Declare the 13 significant characters only - the 2-character control key printed on the card is NOT part of this rubrique.<br><br>Norm definition, CT2026.1.2, quoted verbatim: « Le numéro d'inscription au répertoire (NIR) est l'identifiant unique et invariable des individus inscrits au répertoire national d'identification des personnes physiques (RNIPP). Ce numéro correspond au numéro de sécurité sociale. Ce numéro est composé de 13 chiffres et d'une clé de 2 chiffres. La clé n'est pas à déclarer dans cette rubrique. Cette rubrique permet la déclaration du NIA (numéro d'immatriculation d'attente attribué par les organismes de protection sociale) en l'absence de NIR. Le NIA est constitué comme un NIR dans l'attente d'être certifié (circulaire DSS/sd4c N° 2012-213 du 1er juin 2012). Le Nir doit avoir la forme SAAMMDDCCCNNN avec : S = sexe de la personne physique doit être égal à 1 ou 2 AA = année de naissance de la personne physique doit être comprise entre 00 et 99 MM = mois de naissance de la personne physique doit être compris entre 01 et 12 ou entre 30 et 42 ou entre 50 et 99 ou égal à 20 DD = département de naissance de la personne physique doit être compris entre 01 et 99 ou être égal à 2A ou 2B CCC = commune de naissance de la personne physique doit être comprise entre 001 et 999 NNN = numéro d'inscription la personne physique au registre d'état civil doit être compris entre 001 et 999 ATTENTION : Un NIR ne peut être présent qu'une seule fois dans la déclaration, il doit être unique pour permettre la traçabilité et l'identification de l'individu. Si l'immatriculation est provisoire, ne pas utiliser les numéros provisoires reconnaissables par leur premier caractère égal à 7 ou 8, mais utiliser le NIA qui a été notifié. En l'absence de NIR ou de NIA, il est obligatoire de remplir la rubrique Numéro technique temporaire (S21.G00.30.020). »<br><br>Composite key, 13 characters: position 1 sex (1 male, 2 female), positions 2-3 year of birth, positions 4-5 month of birth, positions 6-7 department of birth, positions 8-10 municipality of birth, positions 11-13 birth sequence number. The 2-digit control key that completes the printed 15-character social security number is NOT declared here. Sourced from the employee's social security card and certified back by the identification return; persists for life, and changes only on a state civil-status correction, which is then carried in the S21.G00.31 change block.<br><br>Composite Key Structure. The NIR is not an opaque number: its 13 significant digits decompose as S(1) sex, 1 male / 2 female - YY(2) year of birth - MM(2) month of birth - DD(2) INSEE department of birth, Corsica coded 2A and 2B and 99 for a birth abroad - CCC(3) INSEE commune code - OOO(3) order number within that commune and month. A 2-digit control key, 97 minus (the 13-digit number modulo 97), is held alongside it for capture validation but is NOT transmitted in this rubrique. Sub-field source: INSEE RNIPP. Persistence: allocated once for life and never reissued. ## Sheet: `File Structure`

_113 rows x 1 columns._

```text
DSN Signalement Arret de travail et Signalement Reprise suite a arret de travail — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

═══ FILE FORMAT ═══
Norm            : NEODeS, cahier technique CT2026.1.2 (P26V01,
revision 20251224, release 2026.1.0.9).
Physical form   : a flat text file, one rubrique per record. The norm
states the record layout as  [Sxx.Gyy.zz.aaa,'value']
and gives as its own example:
S21.G00.06.001,'332975200'
There is no XML, no XSD and no fixed-width layout.
A build that assumes XML here is wrong.
Field separator : the comma, hex 2C.
Value delimiter : the apostrophe, hex 27, on both sides of the value.
Record delimiter: CR-LF (hex 0D0A) or LF (hex 0A) alone. Both accepted.
Encoding        : ISO/IEC 8859-1 (E), alphabet Latin-1. Named by the norm
as THE usable character table - not UTF-8.
Extension       : .txt (also accepted inside a .zip for bulk deposit).
Record length   : variable, maximum 256 ASCII characters per record.
The per-value length constraint is the rubrique's own,
from its data type.
(cahier technique CT2026.1.2, section 3, p.77)
Declaration     : nature '04 - Signalement Arret de travail'
carried in S20.G00.05.001.

═══ STRUCTURAL HIERARCHY ═══
The file is a strict nesting of blocks. A child block may only appear
inside its parent, and the cardinality shown is the norm's own.

S10.G00.00  Envoi                                   {1,1}
S10.G00.01  Emetteur                              {1,1}
S10.G00.02  Contact Emetteur                      {1,1}
S20.G00.05  Declaration                           {1,*}
S21.G00.06  Entreprise                          {1,1}
S21.G00.11  Etablissement                     {1,*}
S21.G00.30  Individu                        {0,*}
S21.G00.40  Contrat                       {1,*}
S21.G00.50  Versement individu          {1,*}
S21.G00.51  Remuneration              {0,*}
S21.G00.78  Base assujettie           {0,*}
S21.G00.81  Cotisation individuelle {0,*}
S21.G00.22  Bordereau de cotisation due     {0,*}
S21.G00.23  Cotisation agregee            {0,*}
S21.G00.20  Versement organisme             {0,*}
S90.G00.90  Total de l'envoi                        {1,1}

The exact block set carried by THIS declaration nature is the one
listed on the spec sheet; blocks the norm forbids for this nature are
shown there as excluded rather than omitted.

═══ TRANSMISSION AND CHANNEL ═══
Channel  : file_upload - a file generated by the payroll software and
deposited on the portal, or sent machine-to-machine via the
same platform's API.
Portal   : net-entreprises.fr, operated by GIP-MDS.
https://www.net-entreprises.fr/
Deposit  : S10.G00.00.007 = '01 - Net-entreprises'. Value '02 - MSA' is
the agricultural channel and is out of scope for this build.
Test mode: S10.G00.00.005 = '01 - envoi fichier test' routes the file
to the test environment. Conformity is proved with the free
self-check tool before going live; there is no product
certification for France (FR-CCG-001 Module 10.4).
Mandate  : a service provider filing on a client's behalf must be
registered on net-entreprises.fr and hold the client's
mandate. That is a registration, not a software approval.

═══ THE SEVEN RUBRIQUES THAT DIFFER BETWEEN THE TWO NATURES ═══
Eleven of the twelve blocks are identical in nature 04 and in
nature 05. Every structural difference between the two signals is
in the work-stoppage block S21.G00.60, and it is exactly these
seven rubriques:

rubrique                             nature 04    nature 05
-----------------------------------  -----------  --------------
S21.G00.60.004  Subrogation          O mandatory  I FORBIDDEN
S21.G00.60.005  Debut de subrogation C condition. I FORBIDDEN
S21.G00.60.006  Fin de subrogation   C condition. I FORBIDDEN
S21.G00.60.007  IBAN                 C condition. I FORBIDDEN
S21.G00.60.008  BIC                  C condition. I FORBIDDEN
S21.G00.60.010  Date de la reprise   C condition. O mandatory
S21.G00.60.011  Motif de la reprise  C condition. O mandatory

'I' is the norm's own usage code for interdit - forbidden.
Populating a forbidden rubrique is a structure rejection on deposit,
not a warning.

The asymmetry is substantive rather than technical: subrogation is
requested when the stoppage opens, and the resumption signal has no
power to open, extend or vary it. A single shared code path that
emits 'the stoppage record set' and varies only the nature code is
therefore rejected on every resumption.

═══ WHAT THESE SIGNALS DO NOT CARRY ═══
Neither nature contains a single amount rubrique.

The employer declares WHO, WHEN, WHY and WHERE TO PAY. The fund
computes the daily benefits itself, from the pay history it already
holds through the monthly DSN. Consequences:

- There is no benefit amount to reconcile in this file.
- The amounts appear later, in the BPIJ return (FR-CPAM-003),
which is the only place the employer sees what was paid.
- Where the employer is NOT subrogated it still needs the benefit
amount to compute its top-up, and must obtain it from outside
payroll. That is the origin of most retrospective sickness
adjustments in French payroll.

Also NOT carried here, and each a separate obligation:
- the work-accident declaration, FR-CPAM-002, due within 48 hours
on its own clock and NOT discharged by a stoppage signal that
carries an occupational reason;
- the employer's salary top-up, a payroll amount reported in the
monthly FR-DSN-001;
- the absence itself as a period, also FR-DSN-001.
```

## Sheet: `Population Rules`

_21 rows x 5 columns._

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Declaration nature | S20.G00.05.001 | Filing component | Must be '04 - Signalement Arret de travail' for a stoppage and '05 - Signalement Reprise suite a arret de travail' for a resumption. These are two distinct natures with two distinct field sets; the component must select the field set from the nature, not emit one set and vary the nature code. The 2026 enumeration of this rubrique holds seven values and is reproduced verbatim on the Field Options sheet. | The failure mode is silent at build time and loud at deposit: emitting the stoppage field set under nature 05 populates five rubriques the norm forbids there, and the rejection names the first forbidden field rather than the cause. |
| Reason for the stoppage | S21.G00.60.001 | HR or absence-management system, mapped to the norm's code list | One of the published reason codes, reproduced on the Field Options sheet. It must be mapped explicitly from the client's own absence types and signed off by the client. It cannot be defaulted to '01 - maladie' because the reason determines the waiting period, the benefit rate, whether the absence counts against the employer's occupational-risk record, and whether the top-up obligation is the ordinary one or the enhanced occupational-risk one. | The five [FP] public-service reasons in the list are out of scope for this build. They are shown rather than removed so that a reader can see they were considered. |
| Last day actually worked | S21.G00.60.002 | Time and attendance, reconciled against payroll | Normally the day BEFORE the prescription begins. The norm states an exception in terms: where the stoppage is prescribed on a day the employee worked, the last day worked is the date of the stoppage itself. A component that always subtracts one day is therefore wrong for every stoppage prescribed mid-shift, which is a large share of them. | The norm reserves further exceptions to consignes issued outside the cahier technique, so this rubrique must be reviewed against current consignes at implementation rather than fixed once. |
| Forecast end date | S21.G00.60.003 | The medical certificate | The end date the doctor prescribed. The norm requires it to be populated EVEN WHERE THE EMPLOYEE DOES NOT RETURN - it is the forecast, not the outcome. It is also the reference against which the need for a resumption signal is judged. | Do not overwrite it when the actual return turns out to be different: the actual return goes in S21.G00.60.010 and the two rubriques are deliberately distinct. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Forbidden fields in the resumption signal | S21.G00.60.004 to .008 | Filing component | The norm marks the subrogation flag, the two subrogation dates, the IBAN and the BIC as FORBIDDEN in nature 05. Populating any of them in a resumption signal is a structure rejection, not a warning. This is the only structural difference between the two natures, and it is the one a shared code path will get wrong. | The reason is substantive rather than technical: subrogation is a request made when the stoppage opens, and the resumption signal has no power to open, extend or vary it. |
| Mandatory fields in the resumption signal | S21.G00.60.010 and .011 | Payroll and HR | The actual date of return and the reason for the return are conditional in nature 04 and MANDATORY in nature 05. A resumption signal without them cannot close the benefit period, which is its only purpose. | Where the return is already known when the stoppage is signalled, populating both in nature 04 can remove the need for a separate resumption signal - confirm the client's rule. |
| Subrogation dates bounded by the stoppage | S21.G00.60.005 and .006 against .002 and .003 | Payroll | The subrogation period must fall inside the stoppage. Its maximum length is not set by the norm at all - the norm states in terms that it is set by the employee's collective agreement or branch agreement. A payroll configured with a single global subrogation duration will over-claim for some populations and under-claim for others. | Where the subrogation end date is reached while the stoppage continues, the fund reverts to paying the employee directly from that date - and the payslip must change accordingly on the same date, which is the point clients most often miss. |
| The IBAN is the employer's | S21.G00.60.007 and .008 | Client bank master data | The norm defines this rubrique as the code IBAN OF THE EMPLOYER. Under subrogation the fund reimburses the employer, so populating the employee's account - the account payroll already holds for net pay - sends the daily benefits to the employee while the employer maintains their salary, and the employer is out of pocket twice over. | Where several establishments are grouped for payment the centralising SIRET in S21.G00.60.600 must also be populated, or the fund settles per establishment. |
| ═══ AMOUNT FORMAT RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Dates | Every date rubrique in both natures | Filing component | DDMMYYYY, eight characters, no separators, per the norm's own Date_JJMMAAAA data type reproduced in column J. Note that these signals carry NO amount rubriques at all: the employer declares facts and dates, and the fund computes the money. That is the structural difference from the monthly declaration. | Because there are no amounts, the usual two-decimal and rounding rules do not arise here - which is itself worth stating, since a developer arriving from FR-DSN-001 will look for them. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| What subrogation does to the payslip | S21.G00.60.004 | Payroll configuration, per client and per population | Subrogated: the employer maintains the salary in full or in part, receives the daily benefits from the fund, and the payslip shows the maintained salary with the benefits offset against the employer's top-up. Not subrogated: the fund pays the employee directly, and the employer pays only the difference between the guaranteed amount and the benefits the employee receives, which means payroll must know the benefit amount it did not compute. The value declared in this signal and the payroll configuration must be the same value, read from one place. | The commonest defect is a client whose practice varies by collective agreement or by category while the payroll holds a single company-level flag. Confirm the granularity before configuring, because a wrong subrogation flag is not a reporting error - it mispays the employee. |
| Where the benefit amount comes from when not subrogated | Employer top-up computation | FR-CPAM-003 (BPIJ) and employee declaration | When the employer is not subrogated it still has to compute a top-up net of the daily benefits, which it does not receive. In practice the amount is taken from the BPIJ return where the client receives one, or from the employee's own benefit statement. The engine must therefore hold a benefit amount whose provenance is external, dated, and sometimes late - and must be able to regularise a prior period when it arrives. | This is the mechanism behind most retrospective sickness adjustments in French payroll. A design that assumes the benefit amount is known in the month of the absence will produce corrections it cannot explain. |
| The net social amount during an absence | Monthly DSN, not here | Payroll | Subrogated daily benefits received by the employer are not employer-paid remuneration and must not be treated as ordinary salary when the net social amount and the net taxable amount are computed for the monthly declaration and the payslip. Their treatment is settled in FR-DSN-001 and in the payslip artifact, but the fact pattern originates in this signal. | Cross-check at implementation: an employee absent a full month under subrogation should not show a net social amount computed as though the maintained salary were entirely employer remuneration. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Bidirectional constraint | S21.G00.60.004 (subrogation) <-> S21.G00.60.005 / .006 / .007 / .008 | Payroll | The subrogation dates, the IBAN and the BIC are conditional on the subrogation flag being '01 - oui'. Each of them names the flag in its Conditional Reason and the flag carries the back-reference, so the constraint reads correctly from either end. In nature 05 all five are forbidden outright, which the spec sheet states on each row rather than in a footnote. | Declaring subrogation without the bank details leaves the fund with a payment it cannot make, and the failure surfaces as an unpaid reimbursement weeks later rather than as a rejection. |
| Bidirectional constraint | S21.G00.60.001 (reason) <-> S21.G00.60.012 (accident date) | HSE and HR | The date of the accident or of the first medical finding is conditional on the stoppage reason being an occupational one - a work accident, a commuting accident or an occupational disease. The reason field carries the back-reference. The datum normally lives with HSE rather than with payroll, which is why it is the field most often missing at the five-day deadline. | For an occupational risk this signal does NOT replace the separate accident declaration on its 48-hour clock (FR-CPAM-002). Two obligations, two deadlines, and the shorter one usually falls first. |
| Bidirectional constraint | S21.G00.60.003 (forecast end) <-> S21.G00.60.010 (actual return) | Payroll and HR | The two dates are deliberately distinct and the norm says so in terms. The forecast end is what the doctor prescribed; the actual return is the first day worked and paid after the stoppage. Their relationship is what decides whether a resumption signal is due. | Copying the forecast into the actual return closes the entitlement on a day the employee may not have worked, and the fund reconciles it against the pay it later sees. |

## Sheet: `Example Analysis`

_22 rows x 4 columns._

**DSN Signalement Arret de travail et Signalement Reprise suite a arret de travail — EXAMPLE FILE ANALYSIS**

| Raw Value | Field Name | Interpretation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| ═══ SIGNAL ENVELOPE ═══ |  |  |  |
| S20.G00.05.001,'04' | Nature de la declaration (S20.G00.05.001) | '04 - Signalement Arret de travail'. A stoppage signal. | A resumption would carry '05' AND a different field set - not the same records with the nature changed. |
| S20.G00.05.005,'01032026' | Date du mois principal declare | The signal attaches to the March 2026 payroll month. | An event signal still carries a principal declared month. |
| ═══ WHO IS ABSENT ═══ |  |  |  |
| S21.G00.30.001,'1850175116017' | NIR (S21.G00.30.001) | The absent employee's social security number. | ILLUSTRATIVE value. It must be the NIR already known to the fund, or the signal cannot be attached to an insured person. |
| S21.G00.40.009,'CT-2024-000417' | Numero du contrat (S21.G00.40.009) | The contract the absence attaches to. | An employee with two contracts at the same employer has two entitlements; the contract number is what keeps them apart. |
| ═══ THE STOPPAGE ═══ |  |  |  |
| S21.G00.60.001,'01' | Motif de l'arret (S21.G00.60.001) | '01 - maladie'. Ordinary sickness. | Reason 06 would make this an occupational risk, with a different benefit rate, no waiting period and an additional 48-hour declaration obligation. |
| S21.G00.60.002,'09032026' | Date du dernier jour travaille (S21.G00.60.002) | The employee last worked on 9 March; the prescription runs from 10 March. | Had the stoppage been prescribed during the working day of 10 March, this rubrique would carry 10 March, not 9 March - the norm's own exception. |
| S21.G00.60.003,'23032026' | Date de fin previsionnelle (S21.G00.60.003) | The doctor prescribed a stoppage to 23 March. | Required even if the employee never returns. |
| ═══ SUBROGATION - THE FIELDS THAT CHANGE THE PAYSLIP ═══ |  |  |  |
| S21.G00.60.004,'01' | Subrogation (S21.G00.60.004) | '01 - oui'. The employer is subrogated: the fund will pay the daily benefits to the EMPLOYER and the employer maintains the salary. | Had this been '02 - non', the fund would pay the employee direct, the four rubriques below would be absent, and the payslip would show a reduced salary plus an employer top-up. |
| S21.G00.60.005,'10032026' | Date de debut de subrogation | Subrogation runs from the first day of the stoppage. | Must fall inside the stoppage period. |
| S21.G00.60.006,'23032026' | Date de fin de subrogation | To the forecast end of the stoppage. | The MAXIMUM duration is set by the collective agreement, not by the norm. A global default is wrong for a multi-agreement client. |
| S21.G00.60.007,'FR7630006000011234567890189' | IBAN (S21.G00.60.007) | The EMPLOYER's account - where the fund sends the benefits. | ILLUSTRATIVE value in the published IBAN specimen form. Populating the employee's account here pays the employee twice and leaves the employer unreimbursed. |
| ═══ THE RESUMPTION SIGNAL - NATURE 05 ═══ |  |  |  |
| S20.G00.05.001,'05' | Nature de la declaration | '05 - Signalement Reprise suite a arret de travail'. | From this record on, the five subrogation rubriques are FORBIDDEN. |
| S21.G00.60.010,'19032026' | Date de la reprise (S21.G00.60.010) | The employee actually returned on 19 March - four days before the forecast end. That gap is precisely why a resumption signal is due. | This is the REAL return date, the first day worked and paid. It is not the forecast date from S21.G00.60.003. |
| S21.G00.60.011,'02' | Motif de la reprise (S21.G00.60.011) | '02 - reprise temps partiel therapeutique'. The employee returned part-time on medical grounds. | This return is paid partly by the employer and partly by the fund, so it changes the payslip as well as closing the signal. '01 - reprise normale' would not. |

## Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

_31 rows x 3 columns._

**Declaration prealable a l'embauche (DPAE) — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY**

**What must be declared before an employee starts work, to whom, when, and through which channel. The governing fact for a build is that this is NOT a payroll output: art. L1221-10 makes the declaration a precondition of the hire, due in the eight days before it, so the trigger belongs in recruitment. By the time a new employee reaches the first monthly payroll run the deadline has long passed - and omission is punished not as a late filing but as concealed employment.**

| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
|---|---|---|
| ═══ WHO MUST BE DECLARED ═══ |  |  |
| Every employee, before starting work | YES | Art. L1221-10: the hire MAY NOT TAKE PLACE until the declaration is made. There is no category of employee small enough, or short-term enough, to be outside it. |
| An employee hired for a single day, or for a few hours | YES | The obligation attaches to the hire, not to its length. Short engagements are where the obligation is most often missed and where the concealed-employment characterisation is most often applied. |
| An employee taken on subject to a trial period | YES | Expressly. The declaration covers the hire INCLUDING its trial period, so it is due even where the employer expects the relationship may not survive it. |
| A re-hire of someone who worked for the employer before | YES | Each engagement is a hire. A previous declaration for the same person does not cover a new one. |
| An agricultural employee | NO | Declared to the Mutualite Sociale Agricole under art. R1221-3, on the MSA's own protocol. Descoped as FR-MSA-001. |
| A seafarer | NO | Declared to the Etablissement national des invalides de la marine under art. R1221-3. Out of scope - a regime special per shared/FR_regime_scope_note.txt. |
| A self-employed contractor or supplier | NO | Not a hire. But note the inverse risk: where the relationship is in substance employment, the absence of a declaration is itself evidence of concealed employment. The classification decision belongs to the client and should be documented before the engagement, not after. |
| A company officer treated as an employee | PARTIAL | Depends on whether the appointment creates an employment relationship alongside the office. Confirm per client and per officer; it is a legal determination, not a payroll one. |
| ═══ WHAT IS DECLARED ═══ |  |  |
| The employer's identity, APE code, address and SIRET | YES | Art. R1221-1, 1°. The SIRET must be the establishment where the employee will work, because the declaration goes to the URSSAF of that establishment. |
| The employee's name, sex, date and place of birth and social security number | YES | Art. R1221-1, 2°. |
| The date AND TIME of hire | YES | Art. R1221-1, 3°. The time, not just the date - it is what makes 'before the employee started work' provable. |
| The nature and duration of the contract, and the trial period | YES | Art. R1221-1, 3°. |
| Any pay, rate or hours | NO | Nothing about money is declared. The DPAE establishes that an employment relationship exists and when it began; everything financial belongs to the monthly DSN. |
| The employee's job title or role | NO | Not among the mandatory mentions. Note the contrast with the work-accident declaration (FR-CPAM-002), which does require the occupation, qualification and seniority - so a client that assumes 'we already told them at hire' is wrong there. |
| ═══ TIMING ═══ |  |  |
| Filed within the 8 days before the expected hire date | YES | Art. R1221-4: the declaration is addressed AT THE EARLIEST within the eight days preceding. The window is a limit on how early, not a grace period afterwards. |
| Filed before the employee starts work | YES | Art. L1221-10, and this is the binding constraint. Eight days early is permitted; one hour late is not. |
| A declaration can be filed after the employee has started | NO | There is no late-filing route. A declaration made after work began does not cure the omission, and the omission is characterised as concealed employment under art. L8221-5. |
| The declaration can be cancelled if the hire falls through | YES | Where a declared hire does not take place, it must be cancelled - otherwise the employee is registered and affiliated to an employment that never existed, and the employer's records and the authorities' diverge from day one. |
| ═══ CHANNEL AND PROOF ═══ |  |  |
| Electronic filing is the default | YES | Art. R1221-5, quoted: 'La declaration prealable a l'embauche est effectuee par voie electronique.' The paper form by registered letter is the fallback, and it must be sent at the latest on the last working day preceding the hire. |
| A file may carry several declarations | YES | The EDI deposit route accepts up to 100 declarations per file, which is what makes it worth automating for a client with volume hiring. |
| The acknowledgement is the employer's proof | YES | Immediate on the online form; by email with an online receipt on the file route, with a reference number that serves as proof. Given what omission is punished as, retaining the proof per employee matters more here than in any other filing in this set. |
| A deposited file is proof that its declarations were made | NO | Emphatically not. Declarations that fail validation appear in an anomaly report instead of receiving an acknowledgement, and those hires are UNDECLARED while the deadline runs. Depositing is not declaring. |

## Sheet: `File Structure`

_147 rows x 1 columns._

```text
Declaration prealable a l'embauche (DPAE) — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

═══ CHANNEL - v2.7 STEP 3.5, VERIFIED ═══
Art. R1221-5 makes electronic filing the DEFAULT, not an option:

« La declaration prealable a l'embauche est effectuee par voie
electronique. »

and provides a paper fallback - a form sent by registered letter,
at the latest on the last working day preceding the hire.

Channel  : file_upload (EDI deposit, up to 100 declarations per
file) or online_form (EFI, immediate acknowledgement)
Portal   : net-entreprises.fr and urssaf.fr
https://www.net-entreprises.fr/declaration/dpae/
Standard : ACOSS NAT/5492, implementation guide V1.1 - covering
authentication, synchronous deposit, polling of
returns and downloads. NOT OBTAINED for this build.
Recipient: the URSSAF of the establishment concerned
(art. R1221-3). MSA for agricultural employees, ENIM
for seafarers - both out of scope here.
Return   : an acknowledgement with a reference number that
serves as PROOF; or, for declarations that fail
validation in a deposited file, a summary anomaly
report and NO acknowledgement.

Status   : CONFIRMED for channel, portal, recipient and legal
basis. FORMAT TO CONFIRM for the record layout.

═══ FORMAT - A CORRECTION TO THE SCOPE MANIFEST ═══
scope_manifest.json records this filing's format as 'XML'.

That is not supported. No XSD is cited by URSSAF for the DPAE,
none was found, and the one PUBLISHED DPAE record layout
obtainable for this build - the MSA protocol below - is
FIXED-WIDTH FLAT TEXT.

v2.7 STEP 3.5 permits 'XML' to be written only where an official
XSD or cahier des charges is cited. This workbook therefore
records:

Channel      file_upload (EDI) or online_form
Standard     ACOSS NAT/5492 - cited, NOT obtained
Format       FORMAT TO CONFIRM vs a real filing

This is a correction to be carried back into the manifest, not a
disagreement to be left in a workbook.

═══ THE MSA DPAE PROTOCOL V7 - A CITED ANALOGUE. THIS IS NOT THE URSSAF LAYOUT ═══
READ THIS HEADING FIRST. What follows is the AGRICULTURAL scheme's
DPAE protocol, published by the MSA. The agricultural scheme is
DESCOPED for this build (FR-MSA-001), and its protocol is NOT the
URSSAF one. It is reproduced because it is the only published
French DPAE record layout obtainable here, and because it settles
the SHAPE question - which is what a build needs to know before it
can even ask the right question of URSSAF.

Use it to understand what kind of file a DPAE is. Do NOT use it to
write field positions for an URSSAF interface.

Source        : Protocole d'echanges DPAE, MSA, version V7
Physical form : FIXED-LENGTH records, one per line, terminated
by a line break. NOT XML.
Record length : 1,273 characters excluding the header
(the header itself carries a length field which
the protocol requires to equal 1273)
Alphanumerics : UPPER CASE, left-aligned, space-padded
Numerics      : right-aligned, zero-padded - including
decimals
Optional      : an unused optional field must carry the full
count of spaces or zeros for its length. It is
not omitted and not left short.
Dates         : JJMMSSAA (day, month, century, year)
Times         : HHMM
Blocks        : En-tete, DPAE, Employeur, Salaries, Contrat,
Formalites, MSA
Transmission  : web service from the declarant's environment, or
deposit in the tiers-declarant space, with a
deposit leg and a return leg (admissibility then
business controls)

Where the two schemes DIVERGE, and why the analogue stops being
useful:

- art. R1221-1, 4° requires additional data for agricultural
employees that the general scheme does not - the MSA blocks
exist for exactly that;
- the MSA protocol carries occupational-health-and-safety data
under Code rural arts. R717-15, R717-16 and R717-16-1, with a
monitoring type (SIS, SIR or SIA) that has no general-scheme
equivalent;
- it carries a request for occasional-worker contribution
exemptions, which is an agricultural measure.

So the analogue is reliable for FORM and unreliable for CONTENT.
That is precisely why the spec sheet is built on art. R1221-1,
which binds both schemes and every channel.

═══ WHY THIS IS STILL A SEPARATE FILING IN 2026 ═══
The 2026 DSN enumeration of 'Nature de la declaration -
S20.G00.05.001' carries seven values, and one of them is:

10  Signalement Declaration prealable a l'embauche

It is a FORWARD PROVISION. Production was deferred and is not
expected before 1 January 2027 at the earliest. Until it is live,
the DPAE is a separate filing on a separate route, and a build
that routes pre-hire declarations into the DSN because the code
exists will not have declared anybody.

Corroboration from a second source: the NEOReS cahier technique
2026.1.0 describes an identity return planned in answer to the
'futur signalement DPAE' - in the future tense, in a document
published in April 2025.

Re-check this before each norm year. When the signal does go
live, the DPAE becomes an event signal of FR-DSN-001 and this
specification is superseded rather than amended.

═══ THE CONSEQUENCE OF NOT FILING - WHY THIS IS NOT AN ORDINARY DEADLINE ═══
Two distinct sanctions, and the second is the one that matters:

Art. L1221-11    a penalty equal to 300 TIMES THE HOURLY
GUARANTEED MINIMUM, per undeclared employee.

Art. L8221-5     omission of the declaration CHARACTERISES
CONCEALED EMPLOYMENT (travail dissimule par
dissimulation d'emploi salarie).

The second is not a payroll matter. It carries criminal exposure,
loss of contribution reliefs, exclusion from public procurement
and, for the employee, an indemnity of six months' pay. There is
no late-filing route that cures it: a declaration made after work
began does not undo the omission.

Two design consequences follow directly:

- the trigger belongs in RECRUITMENT, not in the payroll cycle.
By the time a new employee reaches the first monthly payroll
run, the deadline has long passed;

- the ACKNOWLEDGEMENT is the artifact worth protecting. Store
the reference number against the employee, keep it beyond the
employment, and reconcile declarations sent against
acknowledgements received - because a deposited file that
silently dropped three declarations produces three employees
who look, from inside the company, entirely normal.
```

## Sheet: `Population Rules`

_21 rows x 5 columns._

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| File before the employee starts, not before payroll opens | The whole declaration | HR, on the recruitment decision | The declaration is a precondition of the employment relationship (art. L1221-10), and it is due in the eight days before the expected start (art. R1221-4). That places it in the RECRUITMENT process, not the payroll cycle: by the time a new employee reaches the payroll system for the first monthly run, the deadline has usually passed. A build that treats the DPAE as a payroll output will be late for most hires. | The failure is invisible from inside payroll, because payroll's own first artifact for that employee is on time. Confirm at implementation which system triggers the declaration and how a hire that never reaches HR - a direct engagement by a manager - is caught. |
| The SIRET decides which URSSAF receives it | R1221-1, 1° (d) | Client establishment master data | The declaration is addressed to the URSSAF OF THE ESTABLISHMENT CONCERNED. For a multi-establishment client the rule that assigns a new hire to an establishment therefore has a consequence outside payroll, and it must be the establishment where the person will actually work rather than, say, the head office or the one that runs the payroll. | The SIRET is a composite: SIREN in positions 1-9, establishment sequence in 10-13, check digit in 14. Validate the check digit before filing - a transposed digit produces a declaration addressed to nobody, or to somebody else. |
| Capture the TIME of hire | R1221-1, 3° (a) | HR | The article requires the date AND the hour. Most HR systems hold a start date and no time, so this is usually a real gap that has to be closed at implementation rather than mapped. Use the contractual start time of the first day, not the timestamp on which the HR record was created. | It matters because the whole obligation turns on the declaration preceding the start of work. For a hire declared on the morning of the start date, the hour is the only thing that evidences compliance. |
| Declare an employee who has no social security number | R1221-1, 2° (d) | HR | Do not hold the declaration back waiting for a number. Art. R1221-2 makes REGISTRATION one of the formalities this declaration accomplishes, so the declaration is the act that obtains the number. Declare on the civil-status data - surname, first names, sex, date and place of birth - and pick up the number when it issues. | The civil-status data must be exact, because that is what the identification is made on. An approximation that would be harmless where a number is present becomes an identification failure here, and the failure surfaces later as an anomaly in FR-URSSAF-002 and as an inability to obtain a withholding rate in FR-DGFIP-002. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Depositing a file is not declaring the hires in it | The anomaly report | Filing component and a named human | On the EDI route, declarations that fail validation are returned in a summary anomaly report and DO NOT receive an acknowledgement. Those hires are undeclared. Because the deadline is measured against the employee starting work, and because omission is characterised as concealed employment, the anomaly report must be read and cleared within hours rather than days - and the process must reconcile declarations SENT against acknowledgements RECEIVED, per employee. | This is the highest-consequence operational control in this filing and the one most likely to be left implicit. A batch that deposits successfully and silently loses three declarations produces three undeclared employees who are, on the face of it, working normally. |
| Retain the acknowledgement per employee | The reference number returned | Client document retention | The reference number returned on a successful declaration SERVES AS PROOF. Store it against the employee record, not against the batch, because an inspection or a dispute concerns one person. Agree the retention period with the client explicitly - it should outlast the employment. | Given that the sanction for omission is not a filing penalty but a criminal characterisation, the proof is worth more than the declaration. A client that cannot produce it is in the same position as one that never filed. |
| Cancel a declared hire that does not happen | The whole declaration | HR | A declaration registers the employee, affiliates them to the social security schemes and enrols them with an occupational health service. If the hire falls through - the candidate does not turn up, the offer is withdrawn - all of that stands until it is cancelled. The employer's records and the authorities' then disagree from the first day. | The eight-day window makes this a real case rather than a theoretical one: a declaration filed a week ahead is filed before many of the reasons a hire falls through have happened. |
| Do not route this into the DSN because nature 10 exists | S20.G00.05.001 value '10' | Filing component | The 2026 DSN enumeration carries '10 - Signalement Declaration prealable a l'embauche', but production was deferred and is not expected before 1 January 2027 at the earliest. Until it is live, the DPAE is a separate filing on a separate route. The presence of the code in the norm is a forward provision, not an available channel. | Corroborating evidence that it is not live: the NEOReS cahier technique describes an identity return planned IN ANSWER TO THE FUTURE DPAE SIGNAL, in the future tense. Re-check this before each norm year - when it does go live, the DPAE becomes an event signal and this specification is superseded. |
| ═══ AMOUNT FORMAT RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| There are no amounts on this declaration | The whole declaration | n/a | Nothing financial is declared: not pay, not a rate, not hours. The DPAE establishes that an employment relationship exists and when it began. Every monetary consequence belongs to the monthly DSN. This is worth stating because a developer arriving from FR-DSN-001 will look for the rounding and decimal rules and find none. | The formatting rules that DO apply are field-shape ones and depend on the channel. The MSA analogue on the File Structure sheet shows the shape a fixed-width DPAE takes: upper-case alphanumerics left-aligned and space-padded, numerics right-aligned and zero-padded, optional fields carrying the full count of spaces or zeros rather than being omitted. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| The data are HR data, captured before payroll exists | Every field | HR / recruitment | Every mandatory mention is known at the point of the recruitment decision, and none of it comes from a payroll calculation. The practical design consequence is that the DPAE should be produced from the HR record at the moment the start date is confirmed, with payroll as a consumer of the same data rather than its source. | Where a client's payroll system IS the system of record for new hires, the declaration can still be produced from it - but the trigger must be the start-date confirmation, not the first payroll run, and the two are usually weeks apart. |
| The identity data feed three later flows | R1221-1, 2° | HR | The surname, first names, sex, date and place of birth captured here are the same data the DSN carries, the same data the national identification system matches on for FR-URSSAF-002, and the same data the tax administration matches on before issuing a withholding rate in FR-DGFIP-002. Capturing them accurately at hire is therefore the cheapest possible point to get them right. | The tax administration's identification controls are specific and unforgiving: among the eleven DGFiP anomalies catalogued in the control referential are failures caused by a family name of 'SN', a first name of 'SP', a birth day or month of '99' or '00', and a birthplace of 'SLN' - the placeholder values a hurried onboarding produces. See FR-DGFIP-002. |
| Volume hiring | The EDI route | Filing component | The file-deposit route accepts up to 100 declarations per file, which makes it the right channel for a client with seasonal or high-volume recruitment. The trade-off is the anomaly report: on the online form a failure is visible immediately to the person filing, whereas on the file route it is visible only to whoever reads the report. | For a client hiring in volume, build the reconciliation of declarations sent against acknowledgements received BEFORE going live on the file route. The efficiency gain is worth nothing if it silently drops declarations. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Bidirectional constraint | R1221-1, 2° (d) NIR <-> R1221-1, 2° (a)(b)(c) civil status | HR | The social security number and the civil-status data are alternatives for identification, not duplicates: where the number is absent the identification is made on the name, sex, date and place of birth, and art. R1221-2 makes the declaration the act that obtains a number. Each side names the other in its Conditional Reason. | The number itself is a composite that encodes sex, year and month of birth and department of birth, so it can be checked against the civil-status data declared alongside it. An inconsistency between the two is the single most detectable identity error and it is worth checking before filing rather than after. |
| Bidirectional constraint | R1221-1, 3° (b) nature of contract <-> (c) duration <-> (d) trial period | HR | The nature of the contract determines whether a duration exists at all - an open-ended contract has none - and it caps the trial period the Labour Code permits. Each of the three names the others. | Declaring a duration against an open-ended contract, or a trial period longer than the nature of the contract allows, is internally inconsistent even where the channel accepts it. |
| Bidirectional constraint | The acknowledgement <-> the anomaly report | Filing component | A declaration appears in one or the other. Never both, and never neither: a declaration that produced neither was not received at all. That makes the pair the basis of the reconciliation, and it is why both are specified on the spec sheet as returned artifacts rather than left as process narrative. | 'File deposited successfully' is a third state that means nothing about any individual declaration inside it. |

| 6920Z | Code APE (R1221-1, 1° (b)) | The INSEE activity code for the establishment. | ILLUSTRATIVE value from the NAF rev. 2 nomenclature. Master data, not a per-hire decision - and it must agree with the DSN. |

| MARTIN / CLAIRE / F / 17-02-1985 / PARIS 12E | Nom, prenoms, sexe, date et lieu de naissance | The civil-status data. Where no social security number exists, these ALONE are what the identification is made on. | ILLUSTRATIVE values. Capture the family name at birth, not only the used name - the identification systems match on the birth name. |
| 1850175116017 | NIR (R1221-1, 2° (d)) | Composite: 1 = male; 85 = born 1985; 01 = January; 75 = Paris; 116 = commune; 017 = birth sequence; followed by the 2-digit key. | ILLUSTRATIVE value. Note that the sex and birth date encoded here can be checked against the civil-status data declared alongside - an inconsistency is the most detectable identity error there is. |
| (absent) | NIR for a first-time employee | Left absent. Art. R1221-2 makes registration one of the formalities the declaration ACCOMPLISHES, so the declaration is what obtains the number. | Do not hold the declaration back waiting for a number - the deadline runs against the employee starting work, not against the administration issuing an identifier. |
| ═══ THE WORKING RELATIONSHIP - ART. R1221-1, 3° ═══ |  |  |  |
| 02-03-2026  09:00 | Date et heure d'embauche (R1221-1, 3° (a)) | The date AND the hour. The declaration must precede this moment. | ILLUSTRATIVE value. Most HR systems hold no start TIME - this is usually a real gap to close at implementation, not a field to map. |
| CDI / (no duration) / 3 mois | Nature, duree, periode d'essai (R1221-1, 3° (b)(c)(d)) | An open-ended contract has no duration to declare; the trial period is declared where one is agreed. | ILLUSTRATIVE values. The declaration is due even though the trial period may end the relationship - it covers the hire INCLUDING its trial period. |
| ═══ WHAT THE FILING ACTUALLY DOES - ART. R1221-2 ═══ |  |  |  |
| (automatic on filing) | Immatriculation, affiliation | The declaration registers the employer and the employee and affiliates the employee to the social security schemes. | This is why a declared hire that falls through must be CANCELLED: the registration stands until it is. |
| (automatic on filing) | Adhesion au service de sante au travail, demande de visite medicale | It also effects membership of an occupational health service and requests the pre-employment medical examination. | The effect clients are least aware of. A client booking medical examinations separately is duplicating what the declaration does - or is not filing it and believes otherwise. |
| ═══ WHAT COMES BACK ═══ |  |  |  |
| (reference number issued by URSSAF) | Accuse de reception | Immediate on the online form; by email with an online receipt on the file route. The reference number serves as PROOF. | Store it against the EMPLOYEE, not the batch. Omission of the declaration is punished as concealed employment (art. L8221-5), so the proof matters more here than in any other filing in this set. |
| (summary anomaly report) | Compte rendu d'anomalies | Declarations in a deposited file that failed validation. These hires are NOT DECLARED and the deadline is still running on them. | Depositing is not declaring. Reconcile declarations sent against acknowledgements received, per employee, within hours. |

## Sheet: `Sample File`

_42 rows x 1 columns._

```text
Declaration prealable a l'embauche (DPAE) — SAMPLE FILE
OMITTED - the URSSAF record layout was NOT OBTAINED, and this workbook will not invent one. The EDI route is governed by ACOSS standard NAT/5492 with an implementation guide V1.1; neither document was available for this build, and no official sample exists in FR-compliance/00-official-sources/sample-files/. Fabricating a fixed-width record without the position table would produce something that looks exactly like a specification and is wrong in every column - a C25 audit failure, and a worse outcome than an absent sample. What IS provided on the File Structure sheet is the published MSA DPAE protocol V7, reproduced as a CITED ANALOGUE and labelled as such on every line: it establishes the SHAPE of a French DPAE file - fixed-width flat text, 1,273 characters, block ordering - without being presented as the URSSAF layout, which it is not. Obtain NAT/5492 from URSSAF Caisse nationale before building an EDI interface.

SAMPLE FILE DELIBERATELY NOT PROVIDED - THE URSSAF LAYOUT WAS NOT
OBTAINED.

WHAT IS MISSING, PRECISELY:

The URSSAF EDI route is governed by ACOSS standard NAT/5492, with
an implementation guide V1.1 covering authentication, synchronous
deposit, polling of returns and downloads. Neither the standard nor
the guide was obtainable for this build.

WHY NOTHING IS INVENTED:

A fixed-width record written without the position table would look
exactly like a specification and be wrong in every column. It would
be used to build an interface. That is a C25 audit failure and a
worse outcome than an absent sample.

WHAT IS PROVIDED INSTEAD:

- the LEGAL field set, art. R1221-1, in column D of the spec sheet.
That article binds every channel, so it is the right thing to
specify and it is complete;
- the published MSA DPAE protocol V7 on the File Structure sheet,
as a CITED ANALOGUE - it shows what shape a French DPAE file
takes, and is labelled on every line as NOT the URSSAF layout;
- the confirmed channel, portal and legal basis.

A CORRECTION TO scope_manifest.json IS RECORDED HERE:

The manifest gives this filing's format as 'XML'. No XSD is cited
by URSSAF, none was found, and the one published DPAE layout
obtainable is FIXED-WIDTH FLAT TEXT. Under v2.7 STEP 3.5 'XML' may
be written only where an official XSD is cited, so the format is
recorded here as file_upload / NAT/5492 with FORMAT TO CONFIRM.

TO CLOSE THIS GAP:
request the NAT/5492 cahier des charges and its implementation
guide V1.1 from URSSAF Caisse nationale, then replace this sheet
and re-version the workbook.
```

| FR-URSSAF-002 | URSSAF business return - anomalies to correct and parameters to apply | Compte rendu metier URSSAF - retour organisme normalise (NEOReS) | URSSAF Caisse nationale, and the old-age insurance bodies for which it returns, delivered through net-entreprises.fr | Monthly, following each DSN; plus supra-monthly returns (quarterly, annual, on establishment closure) and an annual reminder | Not a deadline the employer meets - a return the employer RECEIVES. The corresponding employer duty is to act on it: the norm refers to the thirty days of the right to make an error, and states that a body may issue a reminder once an expected action has not been taken beyond a period it sets for itself, necessarily longer than those thirty days. | Inbound file retrieval - collected from the DSN dashboard on net-entreprises.fr, or by API for solutions that support it. The norm's stated target is a fully automatable return, consumed by the payroll software rather than read by a person. | XML, NEOReS norm 2026.1.0, validated against the published XSD with the CRM-Val validator. NOTE: this is genuinely XML - unlike the OUTBOUND DSN, which is flat text. | Social Security Code arts. L133-5-3 (the DSN and its returns), L243-6 and R243-6 (correction of declarations); the right to make an error, Law 2018-727 of 10 August 2018. Technical standard: cahier technique NEOReS 2026.1.0. | Accuracy: HIGH for the field set, the block structure, the code lists and the transmission mechanics - all read from the NEOReS cahier technique 2026.1.0 of 8 April 2025, held in 00-official-sources/pdfs/. In particular the dot-to-underscore conversion on transmission, the XML form, the one-attachment-flow rule and the cancel-and-replace mechanism are the norm's own statements, quoted rather than inferred. HIGH for the delivery mode: the authority's own control referential (referentiel-unique-des-controles-neores.xlsx, version 30 June 2026) records, control by control, how each anomaly reaches the declarant. Of the 145 URSSAF controls it lists, 123 are delivered as a NORMALISED CRM plus the online tool, 18 as a non-normalised CRM plus the online tool, and 2 as a non-normalised CRM only. So this flow is genuinely machine-consumable - which is NOT true of every body's return; compare FR-AGIRC-001. MEDIUM for column L pending FR-DD-001. MEDIUM for the substitution power: the norm states the mechanism and the rubrique that signals it, but the operational detail of the opposition procedure is URSSAF process rather than norm. What would improve it: a real CRM XML received against a real client's DSN, and one real substitutable anomaly followed from the reminder return to its resolution. Channel: inbound file retrieval \| Portal: net-entreprises.fr DSN dashboard (GIP-MDS), https://www.net-entreprises.fr/ \| Source: NEOReS cahier technique 2026.1.0, section 3.1 \| CONFIRMED |

## Sheet: `Payroll Scope Summary`

_29 rows x 3 columns._

**Compte rendu metier URSSAF (retour organisme normalise NEOReS) - inbound — PAYROLL SCOPE SUMMARY**

**What comes back from URSSAF after a DSN is deposited, and what the employer must do about it. Two things distinguish this from an ordinary anomaly report. It carries PARAMETERS TO APPLY - the official headcounts that decide the filing deadline and two separate liabilities - and not only errors to fix. And from 2026, an anomaly left uncorrected may be corrected BY THE AUTHORITY under the substitution power, so ignoring this flow no longer leaves the employer merely wrong: it leaves the employer's records and the authority's saying different things.**

| ITEM / SCENARIO | IN SCOPE? | NOTES / REASONING |
|---|---|---|
| ═══ WHAT COMES BACK ═══ |  |  |
| Anomalies found in the declaration just deposited | YES | The monthly business return. Deposit acceptance is a STRUCTURAL check only; the business controls run afterwards and their results arrive here. |
| Results of controls across several declarations | YES | Supra-monthly returns - quarterly, half-yearly, annual, on establishment closure - reporting inter-declaration checks: cumulative totals, the presence of a datum expected annually, and the like. These cannot be reproduced by re-reading a single month. |
| Reminders about anomalies not corrected | YES | The annual reminder return, CRM 124, which recapitulates the year's uncorrected anomalies and points to those liable to substitution. |
| Data the authority has substituted for the employer's | YES | The post-substitution return, made up ONLY of the data substituted through a substitution DSN issued by URSSAF or the MSA. The norm is explicit that the declarant must take note of it and update the payroll concerned, with NO DSN correction expected - the declaration has already been corrected for it. |
| Parameters to apply in payroll | YES | The RO.B008 block. Currently the headcount figures of CRM 118 - seven distinct averages, each computed by the authority from the declarations it holds. These are official figures and they are not the employer's own count. |
| The withholding rate | NO | NOT in this flow. The cahier technique states in terms that the PAS returns are outside the normalisation, which targets the social sphere. The rate arrives through a separate, non-normalised route specified as FR-DGFIP-002. The norm names the AT/MP and bonus-malus rate transmissions as FUTURE candidates for NEOReS, which confirms they are not in it yet. |
| Deposit acknowledgements and upstream returns | NO | The norm excludes the upstream phase - conformity certificates, acknowledgements of receipt - from its scope. Those tell you the file arrived; this flow tells you what was wrong with it. |
| Summary statements produced by some bodies | NO | Explicitly outside the NEOReS scope, which is limited to returns REQUIRING AN ACTION AND A PAYROLL UPDATE. A statement that only informs is transmitted some other way. |
| ═══ WHO MUST ACT ON IT ═══ |  |  |
| The payroll engine, for a returned parameter | YES | A parameter in RO.B008 has effective dates and must be stored and applied like any other dated payroll parameter. Displaying it on a dashboard for someone to retype defeats the norm's stated purpose of a fully automatable return. |
| HR master data, for an identity divergence | YES | RO.B009 pairs the DECLARED value against the REFERENCE value held by the national identification system, field by field. The correction belongs in the master record; patching the declaration alone reproduces the anomaly every month. |
| A human, for a substitutable anomaly | YES | Because the choice is correct or oppose, and opposition is a reasoned legal act. The norm requires the opposition to be motivated. This cannot be automated away. |
| The filing component, by echoing a CRM identifier | NO | The DSN carries rubriques for reporting the identifier of the CRM that prompted a correction, and the norm says plainly that at this stage those rubriques are WITHOUT OBJECT and require no matching between returns and later DSN flows. The declarant simply carries the correction into payroll; each body verifies uptake at its own level. Building a reconciliation on those rubriques is work the norm does not ask for. |
| ═══ TIMING AND RELATIONSHIP ═══ |  |  |
| Each return attaches to exactly one DSN flow | YES | The norm: one transmission carries one attachment flow, relating to one DSN and therefore one declared establishment. The attachment is what places the return on the dashboard against the right deposit. |
| The attachment flow identifies the period in error | NO | Not reliably. For a return on the last declared month it does coincide. But for the ANNUAL REMINDER the attachment flow is simply the last DSN deposited on the day the reminder was sent - the norm gives that as its own example. The period in error comes from the period rubriques, never from the attachment. |
| A return can be cancelled and replaced | YES | Return type '02 - Retour organisme annule et remplace', with a NEW return identifier. Where several supersede one another, the processing and production timestamps are what establish the chronology. |
| The return carries a criticality or priority ranking | NO | The norm states there is no such notion in the model. Every expected action is expected. A build that waits for a severity field to triage on will not find one, and must derive its own triage from the action type, the level and the consequences rubrique. |
| ═══ SPECIAL CASES ═══ |  |  |
| An anomaly the employer believes is wrong | YES | The reminder return carries a right of opposition, which the norm ties to the adversarial principle and requires to be reasoned. It is exercised against the authority, not inside payroll. |
| An establishment that has closed | YES | Supra-monthly returns are issued on establishment closure. A client off-boarding process that switches off return retrieval at closure will miss precisely the return that closes the file. |
| An individual with no social security number | YES | RO.B006 and RO.B009 both carry the temporary technical number as an alternative to the social security number, so a return can identify someone the employer has not yet been able to identify - which is usually why the return exists. |
| A return concerning several establishments | NO | Cannot happen. One attachment flow, one establishment. A client with twenty establishments receives twenty streams of returns, and the retrieval process must be per establishment. |

Carried in the 'Cible d'action - what the declarant must now do' block of the NEOReS return, at path CibleAction.CaractereSubstitDonnee, 2 to 2 characters.<br><br>Norm definition, NEOReS 2026.1.0, quoted verbatim: « Dans le cadre d'un rappel des anomalies non corrigées et sous l’égide du droit à la substitution, cette rubrique permet de préciser pour chaque anomalie si elle est substituable ou non. Dans le premier cas, elle permet ainsi de signaler au déclarant que, sans action de sa part (correction des données ou recours à son droit d'opposition), l'Urssaf ou la MSA se substituera à lui pour la correction de l'anomalie. »<br><br>THE SUBSTITUTION POWER. The norm's own definition: where an anomaly is marked substitutable, it warns the declarant that WITHOUT ACTION ON ITS PART - either correcting the data or exercising its right of opposition - URSSAF or the MSA will substitute itself for the declarant and make the correction. The annual reminder return (CRM 124) exists to flag the anomalies that may be substituted from 2026 onward. This changes what ignoring a return costs: not a persistent error, but a divergence between the employer's records and the authority's, with the authority's version transmitted onward to the pension bodies. | No - context of the return; read to route and log it, not persisted as a payroll value | Field Options: RO.B004.R016 (2 values) | Not applicable - inbound value, consumed as received | N | Code - Display-only | Per return received | Confirm with the client who is accountable for acting on a substitutable anomaly, and within what internal deadline. From 2026 inaction is no longer neutral: URSSAF corrects the data itself and the client's records and the authority's diverge from that point on. ## Sheet: `File Structure`

_163 rows x 1 columns._

```text
Compte rendu metier URSSAF (retour organisme normalise NEOReS) - inbound — FILE STRUCTURE AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

═══ FILE FORMAT ═══
Norm            : NEOReS 2026.1.0, published 8 April 2025 by
GIP-MDS. The envelope rubrique RO.R001 carries the
norm version and therefore identifies the XSD and
the CRM-Val validator version to use.
Physical form   : XML. This is a real difference from the outbound
DSN, which is flat text with a comma-and-apostrophe
record grammar. A build that assumes one format for
both directions is wrong in one of them.
Validation      : an official XSD is published, with a validator
named CRM-Val.
Forbidden chars : '<', '>' and '&' must not appear inside rubrique
values - the norm states this to guarantee correct
XML processing.
Name rubriques  : six rubriques carrying personal names are subject
to the same character restrictions the norm imposes
on DSN declarants -
RO.B006.R003  Nom de famille
RO.B006.R004  Prenom
RO.B009.R004  Nom de famille declare
RO.B009.R005  Nom de famille de reference
RO.B009.R006  Prenom declare
RO.B009.R007  Prenom de reference
Field lengths   : variable. RO.B004.R011, .R013, .R014, .R017 and
.R018 run to 3,000 characters each; RO.B005.R001
runs to 10,000.

═══ THE UNDERSCORE CONVERSION - READ THIS BEFORE WRITING A PARSER ═══
The cahier technique writes blocks and rubriques with DOTS, exactly
as NEODeS does:

RO.B004.R003

But the norm states, in section 2.2, that on transmission the dots
of a normalised CRM are converted to UNDERSCORES. What a payroll
editor actually receives is:

RO_B004_R003

A parser written against the documented form matches nothing at all
in a production file. This is the single most likely cause of an
integration that passes against the cahier technique and fails
against reality.

Note the limit of the rule: it applies to the NEOReS names. A DSN
rubrique code carried INSIDE a value - RO.B007.R001 'Code de la
rubrique DSN' - keeps its dots, because it is a value and not a
name.

═══ STRUCTURAL HIERARCHY ═══
RO           Envoi - the return itself, carrying the norm version
RO.B000    Flux DSN de rattachement
ONE per transmission. One DSN. One establishment.
RO.B001    Profil du retour organisme - what triggered it
RO.B002    Contexte - who produced it, when, under which CRM code
RO.B003    Validation des donnees DSN - the scope validated
RO.B004    Cible d'action - what the declarant must now do
RO.B005    Detail de l'action - one group per distinct anomaly
RO.B006    Identifiants - which individual or contract
RO.B007    Donnee DSN - which rubrique, declared vs corrected
RO.B008    Parametre a prendre en compte en paie
RO.B009    Donnees d'identification d'un individu en ecart
RO.B010    Valeur acceptee

The action-target level is the routing level. One return carries
many action targets; each has its own affected individuals and its
own DSN rubriques. Route per action target - identity to HR, base
anomalies to payroll configuration, parameters to the parameter
store - not per return.

═══ WHICH RETURNS ARRIVE THROUGH THIS FLOW ═══
In production under this norm, per the cahier technique's own
account of the deployment:

CRM 118   Headcounts, for URSSAF Caisse nationale and the CCMSA.
In production since FEBRUARY 2022 - the first normalised
return. Seven parameter codes: A01 annual average
headcount at legal-entity level, A02 disabled-worker
average, A03 ECAP average, A04 disabled-worker
obligation average, A05 and A07 supplementary
apprenticeship contribution averages.

CRM 119   URSSAF control results - contribution recovery, the net
CRM 120   social amount, the securing of social rights and their
funding. In production since 2023.

CRM 121   Identity return: divergences between the identity data
declared and the national identification system (SNGI).
In production since 2023. The norm records that an
identity return is also planned in answer to the future
DPAE event signal.

CRM 124   Annual URSSAF reminder. In production since 2025.
Recapitulates the year's uncorrected anomalies and
points to those liable to SUBSTITUTION from 2026.

CRM 130   The MSA equivalent, in production since 2024.
OUT OF SCOPE for this build (agricultural scheme).

Three return FORMATS are named by the norm: the monthly business
return, the reminder return, and the POST-SUBSTITUTION return -
which contains only the data the authority has already substituted
through a substitution DSN, and against which the norm expects the
payroll to be updated with NO DSN correction filed.

═══ WHAT DOES NOT COME THROUGH THIS FLOW ═══
The norm draws its own boundary, and it matters because three
things a French payroll build needs are outside it:

THE WITHHOLDING RATE. The cahier technique states in terms that
the PAS returns are outside the normalisation, which targets the
social sphere. The rate arrives by a separate, non-normalised
route - specified as FR-DGFIP-002.

THE AT/MP RATE. Named by the norm as a FUTURE candidate for
NEOReS, together with the bonus-malus transmissions and the
returns on SADV signals. Future means not yet: today the AT/MP
rate arrives through the compte AT/MP - specified as
FR-CARSAT-001.

UPSTREAM RETURNS. Conformity certificates, BAN and
acknowledgements of receipt are excluded. They tell you the file
arrived. This flow tells you what was wrong with it. So does the
PASRAU dispositif's own returns, also excluded.

Also excluded: summary statements produced by some bodies. The
norm limits itself to returns REQUIRING AN ACTION AND A PAYROLL
UPDATE, and says that statements which merely inform must be
transmitted some other way.

═══ THE SUBSTITUTION POWER ═══
This is the change that makes ignoring the flow expensive.

1.  An anomaly is returned in the monthly CRM.
2.  It is not corrected.
3.  The ANNUAL REMINDER (CRM 124) returns it again, and marks it
through RO.B004.R016:

01 - Donnee declaree substituable
Droit d'opposition avant substitution
02 - Donnee declaree non substituable

Where it is '01', RO.B004.R017 carries up to 3,000 characters
setting out the business and legal context of the
substitution that would follow.
4.  Without correction OR a reasoned opposition, URSSAF or the
MSA substitutes itself for the declarant and corrects the
data, issuing a substitution DSN.
5.  A POST-SUBSTITUTION return follows, containing only the
substituted data. The norm requires the declarant to update
the PAYROLL and expects NO DSN correction - the declaration
has already been corrected for it.

Two design consequences:

- The substitutability flag and its context must reach a HUMAN
with authority to decide. The choice is correct or oppose, and
the norm requires an opposition to be reasoned.
- A post-substitution return must NOT trigger a correcting DSN.
A process that reflexively files one is correcting something
that is no longer wrong, and will keep doing so.
```

## Sheet: `Population Rules`

_21 rows x 5 columns._

| Rule Category | Field Name | Source System | Population Logic | Edge Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ═══ MANDATORY FIELD RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Retrieve, parse and act - every establishment, every month | The whole flow | net-entreprises.fr DSN dashboard, or API | Returns are not pushed into payroll; they are made available against the DSN deposit and must be collected. The process must run per establishment, because one return covers exactly one attachment flow and therefore one establishment, and it must run on a schedule rather than on demand, because supra-monthly and annual returns arrive outside the monthly rhythm. Parse the XML against the published XSD for the norm version named in the envelope rubrique, and route each action target to whoever can act on it. | The commonest operational failure in a French build is not mis-parsing this flow but never collecting it. Nothing chases the employer, the DSN was accepted, and the first visible consequence arrives a year later in the annual reminder - or, from 2026, as a substitution. |
| Convert the rubrique names before matching | Every rubrique identifier | Filing component | The norm writes its blocks and rubriques with dots - RO.B004.R003 - exactly as NEODeS does. But it states that ON TRANSMISSION the dots of a normalised CRM are converted to UNDERSCORES, so what actually arrives is RO_B004_R003. A parser that matches on the documented form finds nothing at all in a real file. | This is the single most likely cause of an integration that works against the cahier technique and fails against production. It is stated once, in section 2.2 of the norm, and it is easy to miss. |
| Store parameters with their effective dates | RO.B008.R001 to .R006 | Payroll parameter store | A returned parameter has a type, a value, an effective date, an end date, the DSN rubrique it relates to and the date it was computed. All six matter. Store it as a dated parameter and apply it from its effective date; do not overwrite an existing value without keeping the history, because the computation date is what settles which of two returned values is the later one. | The headcount parameters decide the DSN filing deadline, the disabled-worker liability threshold and the supplementary apprenticeship contribution. Applying a headcount from the wrong date can move a client from the 15th to the 5th, which is a missed-deadline risk rather than a reporting one. |
| ═══ CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| The substitution power changes what inaction costs | RO.B004.R016 and .R017 | Client governance | Where the substitutability rubrique carries '01 - Donnee declaree substituable', the norm's own definition applies: without action by the declarant - correcting the data or exercising its right of opposition - URSSAF or the MSA will substitute itself for the declarant and make the correction. The context rubrique carries up to 3,000 characters explaining the business and legal basis for that particular substitution. Both must be surfaced to a human with authority to decide, not consumed silently. | Once a substitution has occurred, a post-substitution return follows, made up only of the substituted data. The norm is explicit that the declarant must update the PAYROLL concerned and that NO DSN correction is expected - the declaration has already been corrected. A process that reflexively files a correcting DSN against a post-substitution return is correcting something that is no longer wrong. |
| Distinguish the return type before applying anything | RO.B002.R004 | Filing component | A return may be an ordinary one or a cancel-and-replace ('02'), which carries a NEW identifier and supersedes an earlier return. Where several arrive in succession, the norm points to the processing date and the production date as the means of establishing the chronology. Process by production date, not by retrieval date. | Retrieval order is not transmission order, particularly after an outage or when a backlog is collected. Applying a superseded return after the one that replaced it re-opens anomalies that were closed. |
| There is no severity field | RO.B004.R003, .R004, .R015 | Client process design | The norm states in terms that NEOReS carries no notion of criticality or priority. Triage, if a client needs it, has to be built from what is there: the action type, the level, the data category, the control result, and the consequences-of-inaction rubrique RO.B004.R015. Those are the materials; the ranking is the implementer's. | Do not invent a severity and present it as the authority's. The consequences rubrique is the authority's own statement of what happens if the payroll is not updated, and it is better evidence for a client conversation than any derived score. |
| Identity divergences are pairs, and the reference side wins | RO.B009.R001 to .R010 | HR master data | This block is built as DECLARED against REFERENCE for each of social security number, temporary technical number, family name, first name and date of birth. The reference values come from the national identification system. The correction is to the employer's master record, not to the declaration alone. | The norm imposes the same character restrictions on the name rubriques here as it does on DSN declarants, and lists the six rubriques concerned explicitly. A client whose HR system permits characters the norm forbids will generate identity anomalies forever until the master data is cleaned. |
| ═══ AMOUNT FORMAT RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Long text is content, not decoration | RO.B004.R011, .R013, .R014, .R017, .R018 and RO.B005.R001 | Filing component | Six rubriques carry very long free text: the control description, the expected action, the user help, the substitution context and the exception cases at up to 3,000 characters each, and the anomaly detail at up to 10,000. This is where the authority explains, in its own words, what is wrong and what to do. Store it in full and show it in full. A field truncated to a database column of 255 characters loses the instruction and keeps the label. | This is a real and common defect: the integration succeeds, the anomaly is logged, and the sentence explaining how to fix it was cut off at the word 'the'. |
| The recomputed contribution amount | RO.B005.R004 | Payroll | Where a control has recomputed contributions, this rubrique carries the authority's figure. It is an assertion of what the authority believes is due, not a correction that has been applied. It must be reconciled against the payroll's own figure and the difference explained before anything is changed. | Treating the recomputed amount as authoritative and posting it directly hides whatever caused the divergence, which will then recur next month. |
| ═══ PAYROLL-SPECIFIC POPULATION RULES ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| The headcounts are the authority's, not the client's | RO.B008, parameter types A01 to A07 | Payroll parameter store | URSSAF computes seven averages from the declarations it holds - the annual average headcount at legal-entity level, the disabled-worker average, the ECAP average, the disabled-worker-obligation average and the supplementary-apprenticeship-contribution averages - and returns them as parameters to apply. They are the official figures. Where the client's own headcount differs, the difference is a reconciliation to investigate, not a figure to override. | These numbers have consequences well beyond reporting: the legal-entity headcount decides the DSN deadline (5th or 15th) and the disabled-worker liability threshold; the CSA averages decide the supplementary apprenticeship contribution. Storing them as read-only reference and driving those decisions from them is the correct design. |
| Route by action target, not by return | RO.B004 with RO.B006 and RO.B007 | Client process design | One return can carry many action targets, each with its own affected individuals and contracts and its own DSN rubriques in error. Route at the action-target level: an identity divergence goes to HR, a contribution-base anomaly goes to payroll configuration, a parameter goes to the parameter store. Routing at the return level sends the whole file to one team, which then forwards most of it. | The data-category rubrique RO.B004.R005 carries 23 values and is the natural routing key. Map it once, to the client's own teams, and keep the mapping under review as the authority adds categories. |
| Correct at source, in the right period | RO.B007.R002 against .R003 | Payroll | The return gives the value DECLARED and the value RECOMMENDED or CORRECTED, with the period the datum belongs to. The correction must be made for THAT period, not folded into the current month. This is the same discipline FR-CCG-001 Module 10 records for corrections generally, and it is the error inspections find most often. | Carrying a prior-period correction in the current month puts the contribution in the wrong year for both the employer's liability and the employee's entitlement - and the employee's entitlement is the half nobody notices until the employee retires. |
| ═══ CROSS-FIELD VALIDATIONS ═══ |  |  |  |  |
| Bidirectional constraint | RO.B004.R016 (substitutable) <-> RO.B004.R017 (substitution context) | Client governance | The substitution-context rubrique exists only where the data are declared substitutable; the substitutability flag is what gives the context its meaning. Each names the other in its Conditional Reason. Together they are the warning that inaction now has a consequence. | A build that stores the flag and drops the context leaves the client with a yes/no and no basis on which to decide between correcting and opposing. |
| Bidirectional constraint | RO.B002.R004 (return type) <-> RO.B002.R001 (return identifier) | Filing component | A cancel-and-replace return carries type '02' AND a new identifier. The pair is what makes supersession detectable: the type says a replacement has occurred, the identifier says which return is now current, and the production timestamps order them. | Matching on the identifier alone treats the replacement as a new, unrelated return and applies both. |
| Bidirectional constraint | RO.B009 declared values <-> RO.B009 reference values | HR master data | The identity block is five declared / reference pairs. Neither side means anything alone: the point of the block is the comparison. The reference side is the national identification system's value and is the one to adopt. | Note that the block also carries the employer's own payroll number for the individual, which is how the correction is matched back to a person in the client's HR system. Without it, an identity correction for a common name cannot be applied safely. |
